⟦S1⟧

§1 Executive Summary

Cinamate and LightsKiddo compete for the same phrase — “AI film production platform” — and for almost nothing else. Cinamate (Build 2.7.1-Crimson, invitation-only private beta) is a production-replacement system: a private studio in software whose stated output is the film itself, generated on the user’s own GPU, cut in a browser, and carried through financing, distribution, festivals and tax-credit administration across 28 verified working modules. LightsKiddo (Agni, Inc.) is a production-augmentation system: a coordination graph over the crews, cameras and incumbent tools of live-action filmmaking, whose own homepage repudiates Cinamate’s premise in a single sentence — “AI can’t make the film. It performs the million recalculations after you decide.”

The question this report was commissioned to answer — why is LightsKiddo way behind us, and what are they better at? — has a two-part answer that the evidence supports only in part, and this report gives it to you straight.

Where Cinamate is genuinely ahead

  • Financial-lifecycle breadth nobody else attempts. All 28 module routes were independently confirmed to exist. The span from investor tracking through recoupment waterfall, clearance, tax incentives, distribution deliverables and festival strategy has no equivalent at LightsKiddo — whose public product stops at post — and no single equivalent anywhere in the 318-company landscape surveyed here.
  • The economics of local generation. Cloud text-to-video floor pricing has converged near $0.045–0.05 per finished second; a 90-minute feature is ~5,400 seconds, i.e. $240–270 of pure inference before a single retake, and real generation ratios run 5–20:1. Cinamate’s local-GPU, nothing-uploads, price-quoted-before-render architecture is a moat made of every cloud rival’s P&L — they cannot match a $0 marginal render without abandoning their business model.
  • A capability ceiling LightsKiddo has publicly ceded. LightsKiddo states as philosophy that it will not make the film. Cinamate’s entire premise is that it does (“HUMAN CREW REQUIRED: 1 (YOU)”).
  • A methodological posture rivals will not copy. P10–P90 bands, a disclosed 0.848 budget elasticity, methodology that ships with the platform. Competitors advertise accuracy; almost none advertise error.

Where LightsKiddo is genuinely ahead — and it is not close

  • Everything that converts capability into revenue. LightsKiddo publishes ~10 substantive pages, a named three-person executive team with two named advisors, four named customer endorsements, five case studies, a working support channel with a stated SLA, and a disclosed in-progress compliance program (TPN assessment, SOC 2 underway). Cinamate publishes one page, no team, “PRESS — DECLINED”, “CAREERS — BY REFERRAL” — and its only contact address, concierge@cinamate.studio, cannot receive mail because the domain is not registered (NXDOMAIN, re-confirmed for this report on two independent resolvers).
  • The crewed-production surface. Camera control across Sony/ARRI/Blackmagic, native agents inside Avid, Resolve, Premiere, Blender, Maya and Unreal, an iOS + macOS on-set presence, role-based multi-user architecture. Cinamate has none of these, and a 4-minute sync that is the wrong side of real time for a shoot day.
  • The education channel. An NYU Tisch relationship is the mechanism by which the next generation of ADs and UPMs learns which tool is “normal.” Cinamate has no answer to a competitor that owns the training environment.

The honest verdict

Cinamate has built more than LightsKiddo has shown; LightsKiddo has sold more than Cinamate can currently receive. Neither company is commercially proven: LightsKiddo’s proof is thinner than it looks (its Oscar-nominee testimonial and its NYU Tisch endorsement plausibly resolve to the same undisclosed company advisor; its Miramax “case study” describes one script run on one morning), and Cinamate’s constraint is not the competitor at all — it is self-imposed: a dead contact domain, an invite-only gate, declined press, and homepage telemetry that the site’s own source code annotates as “decorative” and “fake.” Three fixes — register the domain, publish the rigor, and sell the financing-and-recoupment wedge to the solo filmmaker LightsKiddo’s foundry model structurally cannot reach — cost almost nothing and change the entire picture.

The landscape behind the head-to-head is the larger story: 318 companies and substitutes across 14 categories, of which 122 are direct competitors for at least one Cinamate module, 33 rate as critical threats, and an entire category — content security, compliance and union/copyright gates — decides whether Cinamate is allowed to sell at all, regardless of product quality. Every entry, threat rating and price in this report survives an adversarial fact-check pass; where a number could not be verified against a primary source, it is labeled as such rather than repeated.

⟦S2⟧

§2 Methodology, Sources & Confidence

This report was assembled on 23 August 2026 by a 16-agent research fleet issuing 1,233 tool queries: thirteen parallel category researchers, a completeness critic that hunted for missed players and categories, an adversarial fact-checker that re-verified the ~36 riskiest numeric claims against primary sources, and a positioning analyst that read both companies’ raw HTML, headers, DNS records and sitemaps directly.

How to read confidence labels

  • VERIFIED — a vendor page, filing, or primary source seen during this research states it. 252 of 318 entries.
  • LIKELY — consistent with sources seen but not fully confirmed by a primary source. 48 entries.
  • UNCERTAIN — partly reliant on background knowledge or conflicting accounts; treat details with care. 18 entries.

What the fact-check pass changed

Eight claims produced by the initial research sweep were refuted against primary sources and corrected before publication (among them: a hallucinated “Veo 4”; three wrong price cards; two “pricing not disclosed” claims for vendors that publish full rate cards). A further nine claims — mostly private-company funding rounds — were unverifiable and are labeled as such wherever they appear. The complete corrections ledger is Appendix A (§23).

A material caveat about Cinamate’s own numbers

Several figures widely associated with Cinamate’s pitch — a 15.5% disclosed model failure rate, a ~$110 cost for a 90-page feature draft, “cloud billing $0.00,” and a $1,246 SAG-AFTRA daily scale citation — do not appear anywhere in the raw HTML of cinamate-studio.netlify.app (grep-confirmed for this report). What is on-page: “CALIBRATED ON 3,708 RELEASED FEATURES,” budget elasticity 0.848, P10–P90 bands, 124 automated checks, the 2–2.5× breakeven derivation, “RENDERS: LOCAL — NOTHING UPLOADS,” “priced before a frame renders,” and “TYPICAL SCRIPT-TO-MASTER: 09:12:44 · HUMAN CREW REQUIRED: 1 (YOU).” Where this report references the absent figures it marks them (unverified). If they are real, publishing them is among the highest-ROI actions available to the company (§7).

Scope limits

Both products gate their applications behind login (Cinamate: server-side 302 on all 28 module routes; LightsKiddo: Cloudflare-challenged /desk), so functional claims are claims about marketing copy, not observed software — for both sides equally. Third-party press and funding corroboration for the two principals specifically was unavailable during the positioning pass; first-party sites, DNS, HTTP headers and sitemaps were examined directly. A small set of vendors block automated fetching (403/429/503) and are noted as unfilled gaps rather than omitted silently: Backstage, ProductionHUB, IMDbPro, OOONA, Metaphysic, ActionVFX, Pond5, Fab, QTAKE.

⟦S3⟧

§3 Company Profile — CINAMATE

Identity

“The first private studio that turns a screenplay into a finished film.” Build 2.7.1-Crimson, “INVITATION-ONLY // PRIVATE BETA 03,” hosted at cinamate-studio.netlify.app. Tagline: “Old Hollywood. New Power.” Contact: concierge@cinamate.studio (domain unregistered — see §5). Press: declined. Careers: by referral. No public team, no funding disclosures, no press footprint.

The four flagship systems

  • SYS.01 Studio / Local Generation — script-to-screen on the user’s GPU: “Nothing uploads — the render farm is your GPU, and every draft is priced before a frame renders.” Claimed pipeline: “1,842 scenes/objects → 11 angles/scene → 8K neural frames → 12-bit pipeline”; typical script-to-master 09:12:44; human crew required: 1.
  • SYS.02 The Cutting Room — a multi-track browser editor with an assistant that rough-cuts from story order, tightens silence, cuts to music and balances color; exports H.264+AAC; conforms EDL · OTIO.
  • SYS.03 The Money Room — estimates that learn from real invoices, POs and the weekly cost report (budget / actual / committed / EFC), union-anchored fringe math (28/32/40%), Day-out-of-Days-driven cast days.
  • SYS.04 A Studio That Remembers — one shared project state across every room; full backup, one file; auto-sync every 4 minutes.

The 28 rooms (all routes independently verified)

Writer · Boards · Investors · Clearance · Producer · Contracts · Casting · Locations · Wardrobe · Props · Sets · Safety · Timeline · Production · Finance · Tools · Dailies · Today · Editor · Screening · VFX · Music · Post · Distribution · Festivals · Tax Credit · Workflow · Projects

Stated rigor

Sales model fitted on 3,708 released features; budget elasticity 0.848 “matching the published literature”; P10–P90 bands “because a range is what the data honestly supports”; every rate source-cited to SAG-AFTRA / DGA / WGA / IATSE cards; 124 automated checks; waterfall derives the industry’s 2–2.5× breakeven rule; methodology ships with the platform. Hero counters: 21 incentive programs tracked, 36 stage facilities, 6 permit hubs.

Legal posture (notably candid)

“Cinamate generates original synthetic media. Outputs are licensed to the commissioning member. Voice and likeness models are consented and licensed… Estimates and forecasts are planning tools, not guarantees of cost or revenue. Not an offer of securities.”

⟦S4⟧

§4 Company Profile — LIGHTSKIDDO

Identity

Operated by Agni, Inc. (footer) — though the privacy notice names “Light Inc.” and light.inc, a three-way entity ambiguity an enterprise buyer’s counsel will notice. Positioning: “One change. Everything moves”; “AI can’t make the film. It performs the million recalculations after you decide”; “We’re making filmmakers alchemists again.” Named team: Arjun Agarwal, CTO (ex-ADP, Amazon AI/ML); Aryan Wangchuck, CEO; Vanshika Sharma, COO. Advisors: Bill Tunnicliffe (Oscar-nominee filmmaker, NYU Tisch faculty); Matt K. (Amazon Ads). Working contact: info@lightskiddo.com (live Google Workspace MX), one-business-day SLA.

Product

A production “graph” — 45 nodes / 40 links in its own demo — connecting script, breakdown, shotlist, stripboard, budget, call sheets, set, and cut. Ray (breakdown model) pulls cast, props, locations, VFX and continuity from the script “in seconds, not weeks”; Indra (“our own model, generating against your production graph”) adds in-house generation. Change propagation: “Affected elements flag. The schedule re-derives. The budget re-costs. Call sheets rebuild… fully reversible.” Models run local to the production; content is encrypted in transit and at rest; access role-based.

Reach & integrations

Live camera control across Sony, ARRI, Blackmagic, with takes matched back to shot nodes; agents run natively inside Blender, Maya, Unreal, Avid, Resolve; formats .fdx, .mmsp, .mmb, .ari, .braw, .mxf, .mov, .aaf, .edl, .xml, .ptx, .usd; Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Scheduall; ElevenLabs voice. iOS companion plus a macOS desktop app. Facilities dashboard (Radford Studios, Manhattan Beach Stages, Brooklyn Navy Yard; “67% utilization”) sold to stage operators.

Go-to-market

Enterprise-only: “three different enterprise licenses — schedule a demo to see more” (the demo link resolves to a personal Notion calendar). Foundry model: “our engineers embed with your production… Onboarding is us learning your processes, not your team learning new software.” Claimed traction: “Sandbox deployments underway at majors and established independents.” Endorsements: Kirby Adams (VP Physical Production, Miramax), Tatjana Krstevski (Chair, AI Board, NYU Tisch), William Tuncliffe (Oscar-nominated director), Nad Ashaayer (CEO, Lightup London). Compliance: “TPN assessment is in progress; SOC 2 is underway.”

Caveats surfaced by this research

The Oscar-nominee testimonial and the NYU Tisch relationship plausibly resolve to the company’s own listed advisor (“William Tuncliffe” on the homepage vs. “Bill Tunnicliffe” on /team — same profession, same Tisch affiliation), an undisclosed related party. The Miramax case study describes one script processed on one morning. “Sandbox deployments underway” is compatible with zero paying customers. The privacy policy is unedited boilerplate that names the wrong company and domain and asserts the product processes no sensitive personal information — implausible for a platform holding cast, payroll and minors’ data.

⟦S5⟧

§5 SWOT — CINAMATE

Strengths

  • Full-lifecycle coverage, verified structurally. All 28 module routes exist and gate properly (server-side 302, no leakage). The development→festivals→tax-credit span — investors, clearance, deal memos, waterfall, deliverables — exists nowhere else in this 318-company landscape as a single product. LightsKiddo’s public product stops at post.
  • Local-generation economics as a structural moat. Cloud inference floors (~$0.045–0.05/finished second) put a feature at $240–270 before retakes at 5–20:1 real ratios. “Nothing uploads… every draft is priced before a frame renders” solves the two adoption-killing objections — IP leakage and unbounded cost — simultaneously, and a cloud-native rival cannot follow without destroying its own unit economics.
  • The money end is the defensible end. Recoupment waterfalls and jurisdiction-specific incentive ledgers are boring to build, demo badly, and accumulate rules for years — exactly the work a well-funded rival will postpone indefinitely. Nobody else pairs them with generation.
  • Methodological transparency as posture. P10–P90 bands, disclosed 0.848 elasticity, “methodology ships with the platform.” Rivals advertising only success rates cannot copy an error-disclosure posture without disclosing their own errors.
  • Exit costs genuinely low — a trust asset unmarketed. Fountain export, EDL/OTIO conform, H.264 masters, one-file backup. A producer can leave; Cinamate buries this in a footer while LightsKiddo makes the same fact a headline principle.
  • Single-operator viability. “Human crew required: 1” opens the sub-$1M segment that every incumbent suite (multi-seat, coordination-priced) and LightsKiddo’s foundry model (embedded engineers) structurally cannot serve.
  • Real gate, real hygiene where it counts. The login is a genuine server-side edge redirect with no content leakage — a real, if minimal, security posture.

Weaknesses

  • No working way to be contacted — the binding constraint on everything. cinamate.studio is unregistered: NXDOMAIN, no A/MX/NS records (re-confirmed on Cloudflare and Google resolvers for this report). The sole published address is dead; there is no form, phone or social. Every dollar of demand the site generates is discarded at conversion.
  • The rigor claim is self-refuted in the page source. The homepage’s own comments label its live-looking readouts “decorative telemetry” and “fake telemetry,” with a script that “randomizes a few values on load.” For a product whose thesis is “no black boxes,” this hands any diligence analyst license to distrust 3,708, 0.848 and 124 — which may well be real.
  • The best numbers aren’t published. The failure-rate disclosure, the ~$110/feature price, $0.00 cloud billing and the SAG scale citation appear nowhere in the site’s HTML. The sharpest weapons in the pitch are undeployed and, as of now, unverifiable.
  • Zero certifications in a gated market. No TPN, no SOC 2, no DPA, no named legal entity, netlify.app subdomain. A studio vendor-onboarding form cannot be completed with the information Cinamate publishes. (LightsKiddo is uncertified too — but discloses an in-progress program, which procurement reads differently.)
  • No crewed-production surface. No mobile/on-set app, no camera ingest, no NLE plugins, no multi-user roles — and a 4-minute sync that is fast enough to feel live and slow enough to put two people on different call sheets. On a shoot day that is a collision window, not a sync interval.
  • The two halves point at two different buyers. Call sheets, safety, wardrobe and permits serve a crewed shoot the single-operator architecture cannot host; the generation engine serves a solo creator who needs none of those rooms. Only one buyer can currently be sold to.
  • Tax-credit room is behind free rivals. 21 jurisdictions tracked vs. Wrapbook’s 39 states + DC + PR + federal + Canada (free) and Shamel Studio’s 52 US jurisdictions with a free waterfall calculator. The room framed as proprietary depth is a published-for-free commodity.
  • Calibration set is small for the field. 3,708 films vs. Slated’s 10,000+, ScriptBook’s 30,000+ scripts, Vault AI’s 60,000+ titles, OpusData’s 100,000+ profiles — and published accuracy is table stakes in forecasting (Cinelytic 88%+, ScriptBook 87%, Gower Street self-grading annually).
  • The Cutting Room’s AI features are already commodities. Rough cut, silence trim, music sync and color balance ship today inside Premiere (text-based editing, Remix, Color Match), Resolve’s Neural Engine ($0–295 perpetual), Descript and CuttingRoom.
  • Engine dependency. Local generation rides open-weight releases (LTX-2.5, HunyuanVideo 1.5, Wan 2.2) whose newest tiers are increasingly withheld (Wan 2.5: no repo; MiniMax holding back H3 variants; NVIDIA non-OSI). Cinamate’s core capability is somebody else’s roadmap decision.
  • Throughput math tension. HunyuanVideo-1.5’s own published speed (75 s per 5-s clip on an RTX 4090) implies ~22.5 GPU-hours per feature of 1:1 footage — against a claimed 09:12:44 script-to-master. The claim needs hardware specs published or it will not survive contact with a technical evaluator.
  • Deploy hygiene undermines the “private studio” frame. robots.txt points its sitemap at a dead third-party Netlify site; the real sitemap lists two URLs, both gated; asset paths contain literal “undefined/”; a stray “0” renders in the footer.

Opportunities

  • TPN Blue Shield is now self-assessed. Under MPA Best Practices v5.3.1’s four-tier model, the entry Blue Shield tier is self-assessment published to the TPN+ registry at membership cost — roughly $250–$1,000/yr at Cinamate’s revenue, no third-party auditor. The cheapest credibility in the industry, answerable in weeks. (Fee schedule itself unverified — TPN’s site resisted automated verification.)
  • Publish the rigor — the highest-ROI move available. One methodology page: the failure rate, the real price, one fully-sourced worked example (one SAG-AFTRA rate with agreement and effective date, one budget line derived end-to-end) — and remove or label the fake telemetry that currently discredits all of it. Cost: days. It converts the posture moat from blueprint to built.
  • Register the domain; make contact work. Hours of work; unblocks every other opportunity on this list.
  • Sell the wedge, not the studio. The financing-and-recoupment stack (Investors / Money Room / Waterfall / Tax Credits) plus generation-for-pitch, aimed at the solo filmmaker and the pitching producer — the segment LightsKiddo’s foundry cannot reach and incumbents ignore. Lightup London’s own quote (“we pitched a feature we could never have afforded to make”) shows the pitch-asset use case working — on LightsKiddo’s turf, with weaker tools than Cinamate’s.
  • The coverage-industry collapse left a vacuum. Cast & Crew shut WeScreenplay, ScreenCraft, The Script Lab and Coverfly in 2025, stranding a generation of development-stage writers and producers — precisely Cinamate’s writer/clearance/boards audience, currently unclaimed.
  • The open-weight tide keeps rising at zero R&D cost. LTX-2.5 (22B, native audio, free under $10M revenue, “no per-generation billing”), HunyuanVideo-1.5 (runs on one RTX 4090), Wan 2.2 (Apache-2.0) — each release strengthens the local path Cinamate already owns architecturally.
  • Money Room standalone vs. Movie Magic + spreadsheets. EP publishes no price and its store was unreachable; the incumbent budget stack is ripe for a transparent, self-calibrating challenger sold separately from generation.
  • Press-the-advantage moment on LightsKiddo’s proof. Its endorsement structure is partly circular (advisor-as-testimonial), its case study is a demo narrated as a deployment, and its pricing is gated behind a personal calendar link. Cinamate should not concede commercial traction that has not been demonstrated.

Threats

  • The compliance turnstile. TPN/MPA gates pre-release content; SOC 2 gates procurement; the union layer gates covered productions; the U.S. Copyright Office gates ownership itself. A vendor can be excellent and still be un-buyable — Cinamate currently fails the stack at four heights (§22).
  • Copyright registrability of purely AI output. Copyright Office Part 2 guidance (Jan 2025) holds purely AI-generated output unregistrable; no registration means no clean chain of title, which distributors and E&O carriers require. This is the deepest gate and it cannot be bought around — it must be designed around (human-authorship workflow, documented creative control).
  • Union enforcement and consent provenance. Post-2023 SAG-AFTRA AI provisions, WGA MBA terms, state digital-replica laws (CA AB 2602 / AB 1836), the NO FAKES Act push, and EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations — in force since 2 August 2026 — all converge on synthetic voice/likeness. “Consented and licensed” asserted without a consent registry or audit trail is the first question every serious buyer will ask.
  • Frontier absorption of the application layer. Google Flow (Veo 3.1) ships scene-building, character consistency and 4K upscale at $19.99–$199.99/mo on free distribution; Runway ships Edit Studio, node workflows and agents (~$545M documented funding); Sora 2 batch hits $0.05/s. Each release absorbs more of what Cinamate’s generation layer does. The 28 rooms and the financial calibration are the durable part — not the render.
  • Open-weight withholding. The newest model tiers are going closed (Wan 2.5 unreleased weights, MiniMax holding back H3-Context-IR/Regenerate-2K, NVIDIA non-OSI license). If the trend continues, local-generation quality plateaus while cloud quality compounds.
  • The payroll-rail duopoly gives away Cinamate’s product. EP (TPG) and Cast & Crew (EQT) monetize payment flow (0.75–2% of payroll across the category), so the tool layer is subsidized to ~free: Saturation’s free tier, the free Showbiz Labor Guide publishing the union rates Cinamate treats as proprietary rigor, Wrapbook’s free incentive map. The Money Room competes with free products funded by float.
  • Consolidation takes capability off the market. Netflix acquired InterPositive (announced 5 March 2026, price undisclosed) and will not commercialize it; Autodesk absorbed Wonder Dynamics, PIX and Moxion; Adobe holds Premiere+Frame.io+Firefly; Backlight rolled up iconik/ftrack/cineSync/Celtx. Strategic buyers are assembling exactly the stack Cinamate needs to interoperate with.
  • Voice/music markets already restructured around provenance. ElevenLabs raised $500M at $11B; Flawless holds TPN Gold + SOC 2 + ISO 27001 with a SAG-AFTRA-built consent gate; Suno paid Warner $500M and licensed BMG; Udio settled with Universal and relaunched licensed-only. Cinamate’s synthetic-media components enter a market whose terms were set by litigation it wasn’t party to.
  • LightsKiddo’s convergence path is shorter than Cinamate’s. Adding generation to a multi-user graph (Indra + ElevenLabs already shipped) is a feature; adding multi-user roles, camera ingest, an on-set app, real-time sync and enterprise compliance to a single-operator local-GPU architecture is a rebuild. If the two products do converge, the asymmetry favors them.
⟦S6⟧

§6 SWOT — LIGHTSKIDDO

Strengths

  • Distribution and trust artifacts, built deliberately. ~10 public pages, a named executive team and advisors, four named endorsements with titles and organizations, five case studies, a published philosophy, a working contact with a one-business-day SLA. In a market where trust is the scarce resource, this is the asset.
  • The crewed-production integration surface. Live camera control (Sony/ARRI/Blackmagic) with takes matched to shot nodes; agents native inside Avid, Resolve, Premiere, Blender, Maya, Unreal; .fdx/.mmsp/.aaf/.usd format fluency; iOS + macOS apps; role-based per-department views. This is years of unglamorous work Cinamate has not started.
  • An adoption path engineered around loss-aversion. “Keep your pipeline… onboarding is us learning your processes”; “the production outlives the tool — if Light goes away tomorrow, the work stays.” It sells change without asking anyone to abandon anything — the exact inverse of a 28-module all-at-once migration.
  • The education channel. NYU Tisch is a pipeline for making LightsKiddo the default in the muscle memory of the next generation of ADs and UPMs.
  • Disclosed compliance program. TPN assessment in progress, SOC 2 underway — not certifications, but a procurement-legible posture Cinamate entirely lacks.
  • Convergence optionality already exercised. An in-house generative model (Indra) and ElevenLabs voice mean the “we don’t make the film” philosophy is a positioning choice, revocable at will, not a capability gap.
  • A second product line in facilities. The stage-utilization dashboard (Radford, Manhattan Beach, Brooklyn Navy Yard) addresses stage operators — a separate buyer with real budgets.

Weaknesses

  • The proof is thinner than the surface. Two of four flagship endorsements (the Oscar-nominee testimonial; the NYU Tisch relationship) plausibly resolve to the company’s own advisor — an undisclosed related party, with his name spelled two different ways across two pages. The Miramax case study, read closely, is one script processed on one morning. “Sandbox deployments underway” is compatible with zero paying customers.
  • Entity confusion at contract time. Agni, Inc. (footer) vs. Light Inc. / light.inc (privacy notice) vs. LightsKiddo (brand). A DPA needs a counterparty.
  • Boilerplate privacy policy that contradicts the product. “Do we process any sensitive personal information? No.” — from a platform holding cast lists, payroll-adjacent crew data, minors’ details and location releases. Unedited template text under a “production-safe by default” pitch.
  • No self-serve motion at all. Three unpriced enterprise licenses behind a demo link that resolves to a personal Notion calendar. The entire long tail — the market’s volume — is structurally excluded.
  • The foundry model is headcount-bound. “Our engineers embed with your production” caps concurrent customers at engineering payroll and makes every win a services engagement. It buys lock-in at the price of scale.
  • Nothing at the money end of the lifecycle. No investor relations, no recoupment waterfall, no clearance/E&O tooling, no tax-incentive engine, no distribution or festival layer — the entire back half where independent films are actually won or lost.
  • No methodology disclosure. No accuracy figures, no error bars, no calibration data — nothing comparable to even Cinamate’s unpublished rigor, in a forecasting market where rivals publish accuracy routinely.
  • Scaffolding leaks of its own. Public internal test posts (“/ila/@demo/write-path-test — …It works,” by “Demo Creator”) indexed in its sitemap.

Opportunities

  • Convert sandboxes to paid deployments — one named, referenceable production converts narrative traction into commercial proof, and the first mover in certified coordination locks the studio tier.
  • Finish the certifications first. Completing TPN and SOC 2 before any AI-native rival would make compliance the moat its foundry model needs to justify enterprise pricing.
  • Own the education-to-industry pipeline. Expand the Tisch model to other film schools; graduates carry the tool into productions as the default.
  • Exercise the convergence option. Indra + the graph + ElevenLabs is an incremental path to generation-for-previs and pitch assets — attacking Cinamate’s bullseye segment from a position of greater trust.
  • Facilities as a beachhead. Stage operators are a concentrated, reachable buyer; utilization dashboards can pull productions onto the graph from the venue side.

Threats

  • The incumbents own the budget line it needs. EP and Cast & Crew bundle scheduling, budgeting, payroll, residuals and incentives into the same enterprise relationships LightsKiddo must win — with file formats (.mmsx/.sex) as switching costs and payroll float as a war chest.
  • Frontier agents absorb coordination too. The same model companies eating generation are shipping agentic workflows; “the million recalculations after you decide” is exactly what a general agent over production data will claim next.
  • The related-party endorsement is a credibility time bomb. If a journalist or diligence analyst surfaces the Tunnicliffe circularity before the company discloses it, all four endorsements become suspect retroactively.
  • Services-model scaling wall. Every account consumes embedded engineers; growth is linear in headcount while funded SaaS rivals compound. A capitalized competitor can simply out-hire the foundry.
  • Certification race risk. Filmustage already holds SOC 2 Type II + TPN Blue Shield in the adjacent breakdown market; if AI-native rivals certify faster, “in progress” becomes a liability rather than a bridge.
⟦S7⟧

§7 Head-to-Head: The Honest Scorecard

Different races, one industry

Cinamate’s job-to-be-done: “let me make a film without a crew.” LightsKiddo’s: “when one thing changes, don’t let my production fall out of sync.” One replaces production; the other coordinates it. They collide genuinely in three places: pitch and pre-visualization assets (the one head-to-head Cinamate wins outright today), budgeting and scheduling (both union-anchored), and the word “AI” in a producer’s head. They cannot collide where each has ceded ground: Cinamate cannot serve a crewed shoot; LightsKiddo will not generate a film — as principle, not limitation.

Is “they are way behind us” supportable?

On product surface and economics — yes. Cinamate has more lifecycle, a capability ceiling LightsKiddo renounced, a price floor LightsKiddo’s cost structure forbids, and a rigor posture LightsKiddo does not attempt. On breadth of the financial lifecycle it is ahead of everyone in this report, not just LightsKiddo.

On becoming a company — no, and it is not close the other way. Software capability is not the scarce resource in this market; distribution and trust are. LightsKiddo has built for both while Cinamate has built against both: press declined, careers by referral, an unregistered contact domain, invite-only access. A product with more modules and no way to be bought is behind a product with fewer modules that is in a room with Miramax — even if that room, on the evidence, has so far hosted one demo.

The formulation that survives the evidence: Cinamate has built more than LightsKiddo has shown; LightsKiddo has sold more than Cinamate can currently receive. And the convergence asymmetry favors LightsKiddo: bolting generation onto a multi-user graph is a feature; bolting multi-user, on-set, camera ingest, real-time sync and compliance onto a single-operator local-GPU architecture is a rebuild.

The three moves that change the picture — none is a feature

  1. Register cinamate.studio and make contact work. Hours of effort. Until this is true, nothing else matters — every inbound the site earns is currently lost.
  2. Publish the rigor and delete the fake telemetry. The failure rate, the real price, one fully-sourced worked budget line (one SAG-AFTRA rate, agreement and effective date, derived end-to-end) — and strip or label the randomized HUD that gives every skeptic license to dismiss the real numbers.
  3. Sell the wedge LightsKiddo structurally cannot reach. The financing-and-recoupment stack plus generation-for-pitch, to solo filmmakers and pitching producers — self-serve, price published, TPN Blue Shield self-assessment filed.

§8 The Competitive Landscape: How to Read It

The catalog that follows profiles 318 companies, products, standards and substitutes across 14 categories — every player the research fleet could substantiate that competes with, substitutes for, gates, or supplies any of Cinamate’s 28 rooms and four flagship systems. Entities that compete in several categories appear once in full, in their primary category, with cross-references elsewhere.

Relationship to Cinamate

  • DIRECT — competes for the same job as at least one Cinamate module (122 entries).
  • ADJACENT — overlaps several modules without matching the core job (71 entries).
  • INDIRECT — a substitute buyers use instead, or a gate/standard that decides market access (125 entries).

§9 AI script-to-film / generative filmmaking studios ⟦S9⟧

Market read · The category has bifurcated, and Cinamate sits in the thin gap between the halves. On one side are capital-saturated model companies — Higgsfield (a cluster of circulating mega-numbers — none confirmable against a primary source), Runway (~$545M documented; $308M in April 2025 at >$3B), Luma ($900M at $4B, in testing at five of six majors), plus Google Flow/Veo 3.1 and Sora 2 riding free distribution. None of them do production management. On the other side are pre-production planners — Filmustage (Director's Cut $79/mo), Cinetech, FinalBit, Katalist, ScreenWeaver — none of which generate a finished film. Only a handful attempt both: LTX Studio, Melies, MITO, mStudio, invideo's Agent One, and Cinamate. Pricing has normalized around credits, roughly $15–$125/month for prosumer tiers with custom enterprise above; the "~$110 per feature (unverified), quoted before render" framing is genuinely differentiated but competes against free open-weight local generation (ComfyUI plus LTX-2.5/Wan 2.2/HunyuanVideo 1.5), which is the real substitute for Cinamate's Local Generation moat. Consolidation has begun: Netflix acquired InterPositive (announced 5 Mar 2026; price undisclosed), Autodesk absorbed Wonder Dynamics, and Storia AI — a thin previsualization wrapper — closed. Direction of travel is toward licensed-data credibility (Moonvalley's Marey), certification (TPN/SOC 2 as table stakes), and named human leadership. Cinamate's real exposure is not feature parity — its 28 modules are broader than anyone's — but legitimacy: every serious rival has a named team, a real domain, funding, or a released film. Cinamate has none, and its differentiating claims (9h 12m 44s turnaround, 3,708-film calibration, 124 accuracy checks) are self-asserted and unaudited.
Google Flow (Veo 3.1 / DeepMind) labs.google/flow DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
Google's AI filmmaking studio, current as a unified idea-to-finished-video pipeline on Veo 3.1.

Flow is Google's filmmaking front end for Veo. On 25 February 2026 Google merged Flow, Whisk (mood boards) and ImageFX (text-to-image) into one workspace, turning a clip generator into a concept-to-image-to-animated-audio-synced-video pipeline. Veo 3.1 adds 4K output, cinematic prompting, precise camera control, persistent world-state memory for continuity across shots, integrated Foley, and a Director's Mode for granular visual control. Distribution is enormous — free Veo 3.1 generation reached all Google accounts via Google Vids, with Lyria 3 music generation and directable avatars.

LightsKiddo (Agni, Inc.) www.lightskiddo.com DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
An "operating system for media production" that carries one decision through breakdown, shotlist, schedule, budget, set and edit, aimed at live-action crews rather than generative output.

LightsKiddo builds a unified production "graph" linking script to final cut. Pre-production covers automated script breakdown (characters, props, locations, equipment), shot lists with lens/T-stop/framing, stripboard scheduling, and a budget engine with live recalculation of fringes, tax rebates and contingencies. Production adds real-time on-set AI supervision (continuity, script matching), a live iOS companion with call sheets and maps, and role-based department permissions. Post covers AI dailies (slate, sync, color), editorial selects, VFX plate prep and ElevenLabs-based voice cloning for scratch/ADR. It is explicitly crew-facing: it does not claim to generate a finished film from a screenplay.

LTX Studio (Lightricks) ltx.studio DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
The most mature end-to-end AI film workspace: script, storyboard, generated clips, timeline edit and pitch deck in one project, backed by its own open-weight models.

Released 28 February 2024 by Lightricks, LTX Studio converts text prompts or scripts into characters, scenes, storyboards and video sequences, with shot composition and camera-angle control, project-level asset management, and a timeline. It runs on Lightricks' own LTX Video family (LTXV, LTXV-13B, LTX-2, LTX-2.5) plus third-party models including Veo and Kling depending on tier. July 2025 added continuous clips up to ~60 seconds; the platform advertises native 4K and synchronized audio, and covers concept through delivery including a pitch deck. Crucially, Lightricks also open-sources the LTX-Video weights, which is what makes local generation possible for everyone else.

A $6M-seed AI-native filmmaking platform built for creative control — chat-based directing over a non-linear storyboard timeline with multiple generative models.

Flick, founded by filmmaker Zoey Zhang and former Instagram engineering leader Ray Wang, positions itself explicitly against one-click generators: creators direct short films through chat-based prompting arranged on a storyboard-like non-linear interface, with cinematic controls, character management for consistency, scene editing, camera movement control, collaboration and a built-in clip editor. Open-source local generation stack (ComfyUI + LTX-2.5 / Wan 2.2-2.5 / HunyuanVideo 1.5 / CogVideoX-1.5) github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI INDIRECT HIGH VERIFIED
The free substitute for Cinamate's entire Local Generation pitch: open-weight video models running on the user's own GPU at near-zero marginal cost.

By 2026 the open-weight video landscape is dominated by DiT-architecture models: LTX-2.5 (Lightricks), Wan 2.2/2.5 (Alibaba), HunyuanVideo 1.5 (Tencent) and CogVideoX-1.5. ComfyUI is the standard node-based interface for running them locally, and all major models have official or community nodes. Commentators report these open models now approach closed SaaS quality at near-zero marginal inference cost, with local setups breaking even against hosted inference somewhere between 500 and 2,000 videos. LTX-2.5 is singled out as the only open model with native audio-video generation in a single pass, plus the deepest fine-tuning ecosystem (IC-LoRA adapters, camera-control LoRAs, FP8 quantization for 32GB GPUs).

Key features ·  Runs entirely on local GPU — nothing leaves the machine · LTX-2.5 native single-pass audio+video; IC-LoRA and camera-control LoRAs · Wan 2.2 as the quality leader; Wan 2.5 ~30% faster at 720p · HunyuanVideo 1.5 for natural motion and physics · FP8 quantization for 32GB-class GPUs; broader quantization to cut VRAM · ComfyUI node graphs for arbitrary custom pipelines · Free; no per-render metering
Pricing $0 software cost. Hardware and electricity only. LTX-2.3/2.5 ships under the LTX-2 Community License, which grants free commercial use only to organizations under roughly $10M annual revenue; above that a paid Lightricks license is negotiated. Wan and HunyuanVideo carry their own permissive-ish licenses.
Scale & ownership No company — a community ecosystem. ComfyUI has a very large installed base among AI video practitioners. Model releases come from Lightricks, Alibaba and Tencent research teams.
Collides with ·  Studio / Local Generation — this is the direct substitute, and it is free · vfx · boards
Stronger than Cinamate
  • Free vs ~$110 per 90-page feature
  • Same privacy story Cinamate sells (local GPU, nothing leaves the machine) with no vendor dependency
  • Faster model turnover — new open weights land monthly
  • Total pipeline control via ComfyUI node graphs
  • Fine-tuning and LoRA ecosystem Cinamate cannot match
  • No invite gate, no vendor risk, no netlify.app subdomain question
Weaker than Cinamate
  • No orchestration — the user assembles everything; Cinamate's value is that a screenplay goes in and a master comes out
  • No script parsing, shot planning, continuity management or scene-level project state
  • No NLE, no EDL/OTIO conform, no deliverables
  • Zero production management: no budget, schedule, union rates, tax credits, clearance
  • Steep technical barrier; requires a competent operator, not a producer
  • No price-quoted-before-render or cost predictability
  • Licensing threshold (~$10M revenue for LTX) creates commercial ambiguity for growing studios

Pre-production covers AI screenwriting (structure, dialogue, character arcs), storyboarding and previsualization. Production covers virtual production (scene replacement, environment compositing), motion transfer onto any character, and consistent character design. Post covers a Voice Studio (cloning, transformation, lip sync), natural-language AI video editing, sound design and music generation, cinematic color grading and image editing. It generates cinema-grade sequences from a single image or text prompt with multi-scene character and environment persistence. It also sells a full production-studio service in Los Angeles alongside the self-serve platform.

§10 AI script breakdown & AI pre-production ⟦S10⟧

Market read · This is the most price-transparent category Cinamate touches, and the most crowded. Four pricing archetypes are now stable: pay-per-script ($19/script, Jungle's Breakdown Assistant), credit/coin metering (Filmustage coins, Cinetech $0.02/credit, FinalBit AI-video credits), flat per-seat SaaS ($49/user/mo Scriptflow and Cinetech Solo, $45-265/mo Yamdu, $49-340/mo StudioBinder), and per-production enterprise (SetKeeper $1,500-$5,000+ by budget band, Croogloo $19-999/mo). Cinamate's ~$110-per-feature (unverified figure) render quote is not out of line — but everything else about its go-to-market is. Leadership is split. Filmustage leads AI-native breakdown (45,000+ filmmakers, $1.5M seed led by Raw Ventures/Geek Ventures Aug 2024, ~$2.5M revenue on 19 people) and is the only player here that has closed the compliance gap: SOC 2 Type II plus TPN Blue Shield, with an explicit "we do not train on your data" pledge. Entertainment Partners still owns the file formats everyone must exit into (.mmsx/.sex, MMS 6 EOL mid-2026), and Movie Magic Scheduling (unverified ~$29.99/mo third-party intro figure) undercuts nearly every AI challenger. Consolidation is real: Cast & Crew owns Final Draft, Backlight owns Celtx, EP owns Movie Magic + Scenechronize + SyncOnSet, NolanAI rebranded to FinalBit (Aug 2025), Cinelytic bought ScriptSense (Mar 2025). Two warnings. First, breakdown accuracy is commoditizing (~86% claims are now routine); differentiation has moved to downstream sync and to trust. Cinamate's lack of SOC 2/TPN is a category-level disqualifier here, not just a LightsKiddo gap. Second, this category's SEO listicles fabricate products — "SceneOne," "Final Draft Assist," and "Streak by Entertainment Partners" appear in ranked articles but exist on no vendor site and are absent from EP's own product index.
Filmustage filmustage.com DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
The category-defining AI pre-production platform — script in, breakdown/schedule/budget out, with studio-grade security certifications.

Upload a screenplay and Filmustage's AI tags every scene for cast, props, wardrobe, VFX, locations and stunts, then generates a stripboard schedule, AI budget, call sheets, sides, storyboards and script analysis. An agentic layer branded "AI Dude" does semantic search, scheduling and chat-driven edits. It exports natively to Movie Magic Scheduling (MMSX for MMS10+, legacy .sex for MMS 5/6 and Gorilla) and Movie Magic Budgeting 10, and now re-imports .mmbx budgets for AI-assisted iteration. It is explicitly positioned as the cloud-native replacement for the Movie Magic desktop workflow.

The thirty-year industry-standard desktop scheduling and budgeting pair whose file formats every competitor in this category must export into.

Movie Magic Scheduling imports a script, breaks it into scenes and elements, and produces stripboards, Day Out of Days, unit and multi-episode coordination, conflict detection and customizable boards and reports. Final Draft is the industry-standard screenwriting application, auto-formatting scripts to entertainment industry standards. Final Draft 13 added Beat Board AI (analyzes the beat board to suggest structural improvements and missing beats) and Script Notes AI (generates contextual development notes on pacing, structure and character arcs), plus Navigator 2.0, productivity tracking and real-time co-writing with file sync across Mac and Windows. Final Draft Tagger is a companion utility for tagging characters, props, wardrobe, locations, set dressing and vehicles across scenes and exporting breakdown reports — but it is manual tagging, not AI. Owned by Cast & Crew Entertainment Services since 2016.

Key features ·  Industry-standard auto-formatting; .fdx is the universal script interchange format · Beat Board AI for structural suggestions and missing story beats · Script Notes AI for pacing, structure and character-arc development notes · Final Draft Tagger for manual element tagging and breakdown reports · Navigator 2.0, Outline Editor, Structure Lines, productivity tracking · Real-time co-writing with file sync across Mac and Windows · Final Draft Go companion iOS app sold separately
Pricing Final Draft 13: $249.99 list, $199.99 typical selling price — a perpetual license, not a subscription. Install on unlimited computers, signed in on two at once. A Suite Subscription is also offered. Final Draft Go is a separate iOS App Store purchase. Not available on Chromebook; requires Windows 11+ or macOS 12 Monterey+.
Scale & ownership The dominant screenwriting application in Hollywood for over three decades. Acquired by Cast & Crew Entertainment Services in 2016, placing it inside one of the two large entertainment payroll groups (alongside Entertainment Partners). Revenue and unit sales not disclosed.

Cinemata cinemata.ru DIRECT LOW VERIFIED
Russian-domain AI screenwriting-and-breakdown platform with no disclosed pricing, team or company — the closest structural mirror of Cinamate's own credibility problem.

Cinemata describes itself as "an AI-powered platform that covers the full screenwriting and pre-production pipeline" — write, break down, visualize and produce. Users create a screenplay in a built-in editor or upload PDF, DOCX or TXT; the platform parses every scene, character, location and prop and returns a full breakdown in under a minute, then generates storyboards and exports professional breakdown sheets. Beyond breakdown it offers AI-assisted formatting, rewriting and runtime estimation, a comic mode, a node-based visual pipeline per scene, character heatmaps, relationship graphs, AI pitching, cast management and production feasibility scoring.

Storyflow storyflow.so ADJACENT LOW VERIFIED
AI creative canvas holding storyboard, script, mood board, character cards and beats in one context — cheap, and aimed squarely at Cinamate's boards room.

Storyflow holds the storyboard alongside the script, mood board, character cards and structural beats on a single canvas where the AI reads everything as shared context, rather than generating frames in isolation. It drafts shot lists from a script with AI, then lets you drag shot cards from story order into setup order without retyping. It ships 200 creative templates including Hero's Journey, AIDA, StoryBrand and Five-Act Structure. It also runs an aggressive comparison-content operation that ranks the whole category, which is how many buyers first encounter these tools.

Breakdown Express / Breakdown Services Ltd breakdownservices.com INDIRECT LOW VERIFIED
Not a script-breakdown tool at all — the incumbent casting breakdown distribution network, which collides with Cinamate's casting room rather than its producer room.

Important category correction: despite the name, Breakdown Express does not parse screenplays into production element breakdowns. "Breakdown" here means a casting breakdown — the character description a production releases to agents and managers. Breakdown Express is the subscription platform through which licensed talent agencies and personal managers maintain client rosters, view breakdowns of feature, television and commercial projects currently casting, and submit clients to those projects. It pairs with Actors Access on the performer side. Any competitive analysis that files it under AI script breakdown has made a naming error.

Key features ·  Casting breakdown distribution to licensed agents and personal managers · Client roster management with full profile information · Submission of clients to casting projects · Theatrical Service covering television, features, theatre · Coverage of commercials, student films, non-union projects, director's reels · Project submission portal for productions releasing breakdowns · Paired with Actors Access on the performer side
Pricing Not disclosed. Pricing and eligibility requirements vary by territory and must be obtained from the nearest Breakdown Services office. Restrictions apply to managers outside Los Angeles and New York. Most project postings are free to the production, though some project types carry a fee.
Scale & ownership The dominant casting breakdown distribution network in North America, with regional offices and decades of operation. Access is gated to licensed talent agencies and personal managers. Compared in industry analyses against Talent Systems and Backstage. Revenue, ownership and subscriber counts not disclosed.

  • Free posting for most productions removes cost as a barrier
Weaker than Cinamate

Open-source screenplay tooling (Fountain / screenplay-tools / Open Draft) github.com/wildwinter/screenplay-tools INDIRECT LOW VERIFIED
Free parsing libraries and open screenwriting apps that let any competent developer build breakdown tooling in a weekend — the zero-cost floor under the whole category.

A mature open-source layer already solves the hard input problem this category charges for. screenplay-tools (formerly fountain-tools) provides multi-language libraries (C++, JavaScript, Python, C#) for a format-agnostic screenplay representation with import and export for both Fountain and Final Draft .fdx. Multiple independent Fountain parser implementations exist. Open Draft is a free, open-source screenwriting application with professional formatting, real-time collaboration, beat boards and version control across macOS, Windows, Linux and browser. Screenplay Studio covers script writing, character development, scene breakdowns, shot lists, corkboard, arc planning, beat sheets, production scheduling, budget tracking and team roles — free and open-source. Combined with any commodity LLM API, these compose into a working AI breakdown pipeline at marginal cost.

§11 Production management suites (the incumbents) ⟦S11⟧

Market read · This is the most entrenched category Cinamate touches, and the one where "28 modules" buys the least differentiation. Structurally it splits three ways. (1) The EP/Cast & Crew duopoly owns the professional tier: Entertainment Partners (TPG-controlled since Jan 2020, >1M claimed users) sells Movie Magic Scheduling/Budgeting, Scenechronize, SyncOnSet and the SmartStudio suite; Cast & Crew (EQT majority since 2019) owns Final Draft, Checks & Balances, Sargent-Disc, Media Services, Backstage. Both bundle payroll, residuals and tax incentives — the commercial gravity Cinamate's taxcredit and finance rooms cannot match. (2) A crowded indie SaaS mid-market: StudioBinder ($29-$99/mo, bootstrapped, ~21-29 staff, claims 1.5M users), Yamdu ($265/mo flat for 20 seats, Munich, ~10 staff), Celtx (Backlight), SetHero, Dramatify, SetKeeper, Croogloo, Assemble, Setkick. (3) A fast-moving AI-breakdown wave — Filmustage ($79/mo Director's Cut, ~$2.1M raised), Shamel Studio ($23-$45/seat/mo), Studiovity, InteScene — attacking exactly the "script in, breakdown/schedule/budget out" wedge Cinamate claims. Pricing norms are brutally low: $19-$99/month is the indie default; $249-$999/month or $1,500-$5,000/production is the studio tier. Cinamate's ~$110-per-feature (unverified figure) render is priced against nothing here — the incumbents charge for coordination, not generation. Switching costs are social, not technical: Movie Magic's .mmsx/stripboard is the interchange format ADs, UPMs and line producers are trained on; crews arrive knowing StudioBinder call sheets and Scenechronize sides. Cinamate's single-operator design is the real anomaly — every incumbent monetizes multi-department collaboration, and Cinamate has no mobile/on-set app, no TPN, no SOC 2. The market itself is growing (~$6.66B in 2026, 9.06% CAGR per Research and Markets), which invites more entrants, not fewer.
Movie Magic Scheduling (Entertainment Partners) www.ep.com/movie-magic-scheduling DIRECT CRITICAL LIKELY
The de facto industry-standard scheduling and stripboard application for film and television, owned by Entertainment Partners.

Desktop scheduling software that breaks a screenplay down element by element and turns it into digital stripboards which ADs and UPMs rearrange to build the shooting schedule. Recently modernized with side-by-side split-screen views, drag-and-drop, multi-episode and multi-unit scheduling, and 'red flags' conflict detection. Its file format and stripboard conventions are the interchange standard the rest of the category exports to — Filmustage, Gorilla and others all list MMS export as a feature.

Key features ·  Element-level script breakdown · Digital stripboards with drag-and-drop reordering · Multi-unit and multi-episode scheduling · Conflict detection ('red flags') · Day Out of Days, cast/crew and dozens of industry-standard reports · Exports that downstream tools (budgeting, AI breakdown services) all consume
Pricing EP publishes no price on the product page; store returned HTTP 503 during verification. Third-party introductory figures (~$29.99/mo) are unverified.

EP claims a customer base exceeding one million users and is the global leader in entertainment payroll, workforce management, residuals and tax incentives. Movie Magic has been the recognized scheduling standard for decades — no independently published install-base percentage exists.

§12 Film finance, budgeting, payroll & production accounting ⟦S12⟧

Market read · Structure: a PE-owned duopoly plus one funded challenger. Entertainment Partners (TPG, 2019) and Cast & Crew (EQT, 2018, from Silver Lake's $700M 2015 buy) have spent a decade absorbing the category — EP took SyncOnSet, Moneypenny and CASHét (June 2025, 2,500+ productions/yr); Cast & Crew took Final Draft (2016), CAPS, Media Services/Showbiz (2020), Sargent-Disc and The TEAM Companies. Wrapbook ($151M raised, $1B valuation in 2021, ~$750M on PitchBook now) is the only venture challenger at scale; GreenSlate (Francisco Partners, 2023) is the PE-backed middle. Pricing is the decisive fact. The money layer is priced on payment flow, not software: Wrapbook is reported at 0.75-1.5% of payroll, Topsheet publishes a flat 2% with a $50 batch minimum, ABS charges a weekly fee plus percent of gross, and EP/C&C/GreenSlate quote per production and disclose nothing. Float and fees subsidize the software, which is why the tool layer is nearly free — Saturation's free tier, Movie Magic Budgeting (EP publishes no price; third-party figures conflict), Showbiz at $399 for two seats, Gorilla ~$269/yr, the free Showbiz Labor Guide giving away the union rates Cinamate treats as proprietary rigor. For Cinamate: the Money Room competes only on the layer everyone gives away, while owning none of the rail that pays for it — no EOR, no tax filing, no workers' comp, no union remittance. Saturation.io is the closest analogue and already free plus card-enabled; Filmustage ($79/mo) and Rivet AI ($150/project) already ship script-to-budget. Direction of travel is incumbent absorption of AI (Wrapbook's invoice-to-PO matching), and no SOC 2 is disqualifying where SSNs and bank details are involved.
Cast & Crew www.castandcrew.com DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
EQT-owned payroll-and-software conglomerate that owns PSL+, Media Services/Showbiz, CAPS, Sargent-Disc, The TEAM Companies and — critically for Cinamate — Final Draft.

Cast & Crew is the other half of the incumbent duopoly. Its accounting platform is PSL+ (budget setup, daily cost tracking, vendor payment, project cost reporting) with PSL+ DPO (digital purchase orders), plus Studio+ and Reporting+ for studio-level rollups. Through Media Services it owns the Showbiz suite — Showbiz Budgeting 10, Showbiz Timecards (Cast and Crew editions), the free Showbiz Labor Guide of union scale rates, MediaWeb production accounting, TiM digital onboarding and Digital Purchase Order. Through Sargent-Disc it runs UK payroll and the Digital Production Office (Payroll, Payslip, Payscales, CrewStart, Sd Production Card). CAPS Payroll serves commercials and The TEAM Companies handles residuals and multi-medium/advertising payroll. It also does residuals, workers' comp, labor relations, incentive management and incentive financing. Final Draft, the screenwriting standard, has been a Cast & Crew subsidiary since 2016.

Key features ·  PSL+ cost management with budget setup, daily costs, AP and cost reports · PSL+ DPO digital purchase orders · Studio+ / Reporting+ for multi-project studio reporting · Showbiz Budgeting 10 with real-time cloud collaboration on a desktop core · Showbiz Timecards and the free Showbiz Labor Guide rate database · Sargent-Disc Digital Production Office, CrewStart and Sd Production Card (UK) · Residuals processing, workers' comp, labor relations, incentive financing · Final Draft screenwriting software

Entertainment Partners (EP) www.ep.com DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
TPG-owned incumbent that supplies payroll, production accounting, budgeting, scheduling, p-cards, residuals and tax-incentive advisory to most of the studio system.

EP is the largest single vendor in production finance. Its accounting stack is SmartAccounting (cost management, 250+ template reports, ACH payments, invoice scanning, role-based permissions, cashflow preview, one-click audit reporting, UK Making Tax Digital compliance) integrated with SmartPO (purchase orders), SmartTime (digital timecards), SmartStart (onboarding) and EP Payroll. Movie Magic Budgeting and Movie Magic Scheduling are the industry's default budget and stripboard formats and push GL codes and budget amounts directly into SmartAccounting. EP has bought its way across the rest of the workflow: SyncOnSet (continuity/assets), CASHét (purchasing cards and AP payments, June 2025), and Moneypenny (indie production accounting for UK/Australia/NZ). It also runs the most-cited production-incentives database and an incentives estimator, plus residuals processing and production finance/incentive lending.

Producer-built cloud budgeting and production-spend platform with a genuinely free tier — the closest structural analogue to Cinamate's Money Room for a single operator.

Saturation is collaborative cloud budgeting plus expense management plus real-time actuals in one browser product, built by film producer Jens Jacob. It covers budget building with fringe automation and template libraries, cost actualization against the budget (a living budget-vs-actuals cost report), purchase orders and approval workflows, expense cards, and integrations to QuickBooks, Slack, Plaid bank feeds and Wrapbook for payroll actuals. It publishes a free public database of 1,500+ real production budgets and AI-assisted budgeting features on every tier including free. In January 2026 it launched a production charge card for film and video teams, underwritten on production revenue and operating performance rather than the founder's personal credit, with up to 3% cash back on qualifying production spend. It also runs an aggressive comparison-content SEO operation against every competitor in this category.

Wrapbook www.wrapbook.com DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
Venture-backed, AI-enabled production payroll and production accounting platform that has become the modern default for commercials and indie/mid-budget film and TV.

Wrapbook is a single platform covering crew onboarding/startwork, digital timecards, accounts payable, production accounting/cost reporting, payroll (union and non-union, as employer of record) and real-time data insights. In late 2025 it shipped AI enhancements that read uploaded invoices in any format (PDF, photo, scan) and auto-match them to the correct purchase order, natural-language report generation, automatic vendor tax-ID verification and fraud checks, and native vendor payments. It publishes a large free knowledge layer — a state-by-state production incentive center, union rate-card guides (DGA, SAG-AFTRA, IATSE) and budgeting templates — that ranks well and functions as top-of-funnel. In March 2026 it published a 2026 State of Production Finance & Accounting report (100 production finance professionals) and in August 2026 launched WRAPPED, an original video series on production finance hosted by co-founder Cameron Woodward.

Key features ·  Onboarding/startwork with digital I-9, W-4, union paperwork · Digital timecards and hours-to-gross calculation · Accounts payable with AI invoice-to-PO matching and vendor verification · Production accounting dashboard and real-time cost reporting · Payroll as employer of record, union and non-union, US and Canada · Native vendor payments; crew expense capture and reimbursement · Natural-language report generation · Free production incentive database and union rate guides
Pricing Not published on Wrapbook's own site — the site routes to sales. Third-party review aggregators report a percentage-of-payroll model of roughly 0.75%-1.5% of payroll plus per-transaction fees (one aggregator cites ~$18 per transaction as of 2025). Treat the exact numbers as unverified; the percentage-of-payroll structure is the well-established norm and Wrapbook markets itself as cheaper than the 3-5% legacy providers.
Scale & ownership ~$151M raised across 4 rounds per Tracxn: $27M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (2021), $100M Series B led by Tiger Global (Nov 2021) at a $1B valuation, and a further ~$20M round in Sept 2024. Other investors: Bessemer, Jeffrey Katzenberg's WndrCo, A*, Uncork Capital, Equal Ventures, Michael Ovitz. PitchBook/Tracxn currently show a $750M valuation (uncertain). Movie Magic Budgeting (Entertainment Partners) www.ep.com/movie-magic-budgeting DIRECT HIGH LIKELY
The desktop budgeting application that is the de facto file format and layout standard for film and TV budgets worldwide.

Movie Magic Budgeting builds the budget document that studios, financiers, completion guarantors and tax-credit auditors expect to see. It supports up to four levels of budget hierarchy, globals, fringes with automatic payroll tax and union benefit calculation, template libraries in major studio formats, multi-currency, tax incentive modeling and pattern budgeting for episodic. It is explicitly a pre-production budgeting tool: it does not track actuals, manage POs, handle AP or produce cost reports from real transactions — that job passes to SmartAccounting, which imports its GL codes and budget amounts directly. It is sold standalone as a subscription and taught through EP Academy courses.

§13 Sales forecasting, film analytics, investor & incentive tooling ⟦S13⟧

Market read · This is the most crowded and most credentialed category Cinamate touches, and the one where its headline rigor claims are weakest on inspection. Three findings matter most. First, published accuracy is NOT a Cinamate differentiator — it is table stakes. Cinelytic claims 88%+ title-level accuracy across 80 territories (April 2026 launch); ScriptBook claims 87% greenlight accuracy vs. a 36% industry baseline; Largo.ai is reported at 80-82%; Vista/Cinema Intelligence publishes +/-15% opening-weekend accuracy; Gower Street publicly grades its annual forecasts (2024 within 5%, 2025 tracking within 2%). Cinamate's genuinely rarer move is disclosing a *failure* rate (15.5%) rather than only a success rate — but ForecastFilm goes further by publishing every forecast as a low/high range with a confidence tier and grading each one publicly after the weekend. Ranges and confidence bands are also standard at Boxoffice Pro (best/worst case). Second, the 3,708-film calibration set is small for this field. Slated's financial model uses 10,000+ released films, Vault AI 60,000+ titles, ScriptBook 30,000+ scripts, OpusData 100,000+ bankability profiles. Third, the taxcredit room's 21 jurisdictions is the clearest deficit anywhere in Cinamate. Wrapbook covers 39 states plus DC, Puerto Rico, federal and Canada — free. Shamel Studio covers 52 US jurisdictions plus a waterfall calculator — free. EP and Cast & Crew cover worldwide. Cinamate is charging for less coverage than incumbents give away, against payroll companies whose incentive data is a loss-leader for a much larger business. Direction of travel: consolidation (Cinelytic absorbing Jumpcut; Vista absorbing Cinema Intelligence) and incentive data commoditizing to free.

Comscore Movies www.comscore.com/Products/Movies ADJACENT HIGH VERIFIED
The industry's system of record for theatrical box office measurement, 50 years old and used by every major studio.

Measures box office performance in more than 70 countries, delivering theatrical grosses, audience demographics, marketing impact and global release tracking. Product line includes Box Office Essentials and International Box Office Essentials (the reporting backbone), PostTrak exit polling for real-time audience demographics and interest drivers, Theatrical Distribution System (TDS) for release management, Exhibitor Management System, Cinema ACE for digital cinema operations, and Hollywood Software. Comscore data underpins third-party forecasting products including Gower Street's FORECAST.

Gower Street Analytics gower.st ADJACENT HIGH VERIFIED
Theatrical release-dating and box office simulation platform covering 85+ markets, whose public annual forecasts are graded against actuals.

Its FORECAST web application gives theatrical distribution executives daily box office predictions for each market, built from expert analysis, Comscore historical data and the live release calendar, letting them simulate complex release-dating moves in seconds across 85+ markets. Each film page shows comparison titles and a graph of how estimates changed over time. Gower Street also publishes headline global box office forecasts — it projected $35bn for 2026, later revised to $34.7bn ahead of CinemaCon.

ForecastFilm www.forecastfilm.com DIRECT MEDIUM LIKELY
Free, fully explainable opening-weekend forecasts published as ranges with confidence tiers and publicly graded after the fact.

Publishes opening-weekend box office forecasts with full reasoning attached before the weekend, then grades them after it, tracking accuracy in public. Forecasts are issued as ranges — a low and a high estimate — with a confidence tier (low/medium/high) reflecting data availability and comp density, where high confidence means the model found dense comparables. It explicitly refuses a black-box posture: inputs are listed, comprising TMDb metadata, prior-film performance for every named cast and crew member, budget vs. comp-budget cohorts, MPAA rating, release window, competitive slate, and trailer-view-to-opening conversion for same-genre comps. Paid tiers cover script-stage forecasts for writers, project-level P&L for producers, and embeddable forecasts for creators.

Key features ·  Forecasts published as low/high ranges with confidence tiers · Publicly tracked and graded accuracy after each weekend · Full reasoning and input list disclosed per forecast · Script-stage forecasts (paid tier) · Project-level P&L for producers (paid tier) · Embeddable forecasts for creators (paid tier)
Pricing Every weekend prediction is free with reasoning attached. Paid tiers exist for script-stage forecasts, producer P&L and embeddable widgets; specific prices not published in sources reviewed.

Patented global demand measurement and content valuation across 200+ markets, translating audience demand into dollar contribution.

§14 Distribution, sales agents, deliverables & festivals ⟦S14⟧

Market read · This is the half of the lifecycle LightsKiddo ignores, and it is the half where Cinamate is weakest, because almost nothing here is really software - it is a set of transaction rails and service businesses, and rails cannot be replaced by a module. The category splits four ways. (1) Festival submission is a near-monopoly: FilmFreeway (Backstage-owned, free to filmmakers, 12% off festivals) took the market when Withoutabox closed in 2019, with Festhome second and strongest in Spanish-language and European circuits. (2) Screening and market access is consolidating: EditShare absorbed Shift Media (MediaSilo, Wiredrive, Screeners.com, and shift.io now redirects to mediasilo.com), competing with Indee.tv, Shift72 and Cinando, whose Marché du Film ownership and 2026 EU-funded rebuild give it institutional weight nobody else has. (3) Deliverables is a two-layer stack - specialist automated QC (Venera, Interra BATON, Telestream Vidchecker) beneath supply-chain platforms (Ateliere Connect, Cineverse MatchPoint, Premiere Digital, Deluxe, Vubiquity) - all enterprise-priced and demo-gated. (4) Rights and money is consolidating hard: Rightsline bought FilmTrack from City National Bank in June 2024, wound the product down, and now sits at ~390 customers against Whip Media. The direction of travel is toward free or near-free self-service at the bottom (Filmhub 80/20, Amazon Prime Video Direct at zero cost) and enterprise consolidation at the top, hollowing out the middle. Pricing norms: free-to-filmmaker with commission on the festival side; 20% revenue share on aggregation; opaque demo-gated enterprise SaaS everywhere else. For Cinamate this is the credibility cliff. Its distribution, festivals and screening modules are planning surfaces, not rails - they cannot submit to a festival, deliver a package, or clear an avail. Worse, no SOC 2 and no TPN disqualify its screening room from exactly the pre-release use MediaSilo, Screeners.com and Indee.tv own. The defensible play is integration - feed FilmFreeway, Filmhub and a QC vendor - not replacement.
FilmFreeway filmfreeway.com DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
The de facto monopoly on film festival and screenplay-contest submissions since Withoutabox shut in 2019.

FilmFreeway is a two-sided marketplace: filmmakers keep a single hosted screener and press kit and submit it to thousands of festivals and contests; festivals get a submission-management back office (entry forms, judging, notifications, payouts). It is the transaction layer - a film's festival run literally happens through it. It is free for filmmakers beyond the festivals' own entry fees, and monetises by taking a commission on paid entries.

Key features ·  Single hosted screener re-used across unlimited submissions · Festival directory with deadlines, fees, awards and reviews · Submission tracking and status per festival · Festival-side judging, screener rooms, notifications and payouts · Early-bird / student discount handling at checkout · Anti-fraud auditing of listed festivals
Pricing Free to filmmakers - they pay only each festival's entry fee (e.g. New York Film Festival listed a $60 fee for the April-May 2026 window). Festivals pay a 12% commission on paid entries and nothing at all if they charge no entry fee. Search results and the help centre state the 12% figure; the pricing page itself returned HTTP 403 at fetch time.
Scale & ownership Launched in Canada in 2014 as a four-person startup; acquired by Backstage in September 2021. Became the dominant submission platform after Amazon shut Withoutabox in September 2019. Directory runs to thousands of festivals worldwide.
Collides with ·  festivals · screening · distribution (deliverables) - screener/press-kit assembly · projects
Stronger than Cinamate
  • It is where submissions actually happen - Cinamate's festivals module can track and plan a circuit but cannot submit to a single festival
  • Owns both sides of the market: filmmakers and festival back offices
  • Zero cost to the filmmaker, versus a private paid beta
  • Backstage ownership gives it distribution and an incumbent brand
  • Hosted screener doubles as a delivery mechanism, competing with Cinamate's screening room
Weaker than Cinamate
  • Nothing upstream of a finished film - no budgeting, scheduling, clearance, contracts or cost reporting
  • Long-running criticism for hosting fraudulent or predatory 'festivals' that harvest entry fees
  • No festival strategy modelling, no ROI or sales projection, no tax credit or union rate data
  • Basic analytics; it is a submissions pipe, not an intelligence product

Filmhub filmhub.com DIRECT CRITICAL LIKELY
Self-serve, non-exclusive global distribution rail that puts an indie title onto 100+ exhibitors (per homepage) for a 20% cut.

Filmhub is a marketplace where a rights holder uploads a finished film plus artwork and metadata, and Filmhub pitches and delivers it to its buyer network (Tubi, Plex, Prime Video, Roku and similar), handling QC, transcoding, asset delivery and payouts. It is non-exclusive and self-service, so a single operator can release a feature without a sales agent. In February 2026 it launched Relay, its own $4.99/month streaming service seeded with 20,000+ titles, on a 60/40 Filmhub/Relay split with viewership-weighted attribution to filmmakers.

Key features ·  Self-serve upload, metadata and artwork onboarding · Standard QC included on all tiers; Premium QC as a paid or bundled service · Delivery to 100+ exhibitors (per homepage) across 200+ territories · Non-exclusive terms; PayPal withdrawal at any time · Relay owned-and-operated SVOD channel (launched 14 Feb 2026) · Channel blocking / release-date scheduling on paid tiers · Earnings and analytics dashboard
Pricing Homepage: works with 'over 100 of the world's biggest exhibitors'. /pricing and /plans 404; plan tiers ($999/$1,999) and an 80/20 split circulate but are NOT vendor-confirmed.
Scale & ownership Founded 2015; Series A, roughly $7M raised per third-party startup coverage (unverified by a primary source). Claims 130+ streaming platform partners and 200+ territories. Relay launched with 20,000+ titles, implying a catalogue in that order.

Cinando (Marché du Film) www.marchedufilm.com/about/cinando DIRECT HIGH LIKELY
The Cannes Marché's industry database and B2B screening room - the default rolodex and screener rail for international sales.

Cinando is the professional network and content database operated by the Marché du Film: company and executive profiles for sales agents, buyers, distributors and festivals; project and film listings; and a B2B video-on-demand screening service (launched 2012) used for market screenings and buyer screeners. It added subtitle search and purchase in 2017 and enabled virtual market screenings during COVID. In 2026 it relaunched with a full rebrand and a rebuilt platform backed by Creative Europe MEDIA, expanding into TV and immersive content.

Pricing Reported at €149 per year per company for the 2026 platform. Marché du Film and partner-market accreditation includes a year of access. The €149 figure comes from search results citing Marché du Film materials; the Cinando pages themselves returned HTTP 503 at fetch time, so treat the number as reported rather than directly confirmed.
Scale & ownership Launched 2003 as cannesmarket.com, renamed Cinando in 2007. 78,000 users as of 2018 (the last figure in the public record). Owned and operated by Marché du Film / Festival de Cannes; 2026 rebuild supported by Creative Europe MEDIA.

Eventive www.eventive.org DIRECT HIGH VERIFIED
Ticketing, virtual screening and VOD infrastructure that runs a large share of North American independent film festivals.

Eventive is the operational stack behind hybrid and virtual festivals: pass and ticket sales, membership automation, sponsor benefits, on-site and online programme display, DRM-protected virtual screenings with unlock-based access, balloting for audience awards, and a distributor-facing mode for proprietary VOD screenings, branded affiliate links and awards screenings with built-in revenue sharing and reporting. Virtual Single Film: $299 one-time including 100 unlocks, then $0.99 each. Balloting free. Premium support from $1,800/month. Distributor pricing is custom and volume-based.

Rightsline (incl. FilmTrack) www.rightsline.com DIRECT HIGH VERIFIED
The consolidated rights, royalties and avails platform after absorbing FilmTrack from City National Bank - roughly 390 combined customers.

Rightsline is an enterprise SaaS platform for IP commerce: rights management across development, acquisition, distribution and exploitation; inbound and outbound royalty calculation on flexible business rules; financial aggregation showing contract status, revenue achieved and royalties paid or collected; and an Avails and Conflict Engine that determines what can be licensed where, when and to whom without colliding with an existing grant. FilmTrack, long the indie-distributor standard, has been folded in and the standalone product wound down.

Key features ·  Rights management across the full exploitation lifecycle · Royalties: inbound and outbound, rule-driven calculation · Avails and Conflict Engine for territory/window/right conflicts · Financial aggregation of contract and revenue status · Proprietary AI capabilities · Unified platform across content, teams and applications
