§15 Text-to-video foundation models & generation infrastructure ⟦S15⟧

Market read · The floor price for a generated second collapsed to roughly $0.045-0.05: Veo 3.1 Lite $0.05/s (720p, audio included), Sora 2 batch $0.05/s, Wan 2.5 on fal $0.05/s, Hailuo 02 $0.045/s, Grok Imagine $0.05/s. A 90-minute feature is ~5,400 finished seconds, so pure cloud inference runs ~$240-270 before a single retake — and real ratios are 5-20:1. That arithmetic is why Cinamate's ~$110-per-feature (unverified figure), $0.00-cloud claim can only hold on local open weights, and it is a genuinely defensible number if the local path works. The open-weight path is real but narrowing. LTX-2.5 (22B, native audio, self-host, LTX-2.x Community License free under $10M revenue, explicitly "no per-generation billing"), HunyuanVideo-1.5 (8.3B, 14GB VRAM, 75 seconds per 5s clip on one RTX 4090), MiniMax H3 (33B omni, open base checkpoints, stereo audio) and Wan 2.2 (Apache 2.0) all run locally. But the newest tiers are being withheld: Wan 2.5 has no repo, MiniMax withholds H3-Context-IR and H3-Regenerate-2K, NVIDIA ships a non-OSI license. Cinamate's engine is somebody else's roadmap decision. Note a timing tension: HunyuanVideo-1.5's own 75s/5s figure implies ~22.5 GPU-hours of 1:1 generation for a feature, against Cinamate's claimed 9h 12m 44s. Absorption is the existential half. Flow ships Scenebuilder, characters, video-to-video editing and 4K upscale. Runway ships Edit Studio, node workflows, a Runway Agent, MCP, and — critically — ProRes, PNG sequence and HDR delivery that Cinamate's H.264+AAC-only Cutting Room cannot match. LTX Studio and Adobe Firefly (30+ models) do the same from above. None of them does budgets, stripboards, call sheets, union scale, deal memos, permits, tax credits, PO tracking or sales modeling. That business layer — not the pixels — is Cinamate's only durable ground.
Google Veo 3.1 + Flow labs.google/flow/about DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
Google's Veo model family paired with Flow, an AI creative studio that has already absorbed storyboarding, scene assembly, character management and editing into the model vendor's own product.

Veo 3.1 generates video with audio included by default across Standard, Fast and Lite tiers, up to 4K. Flow wraps it in an application layer: Scenebuilder for composition, cinematic camera controls, Ingredients-to-Video, video extension, natural-language video-to-video editing, Characters & Avatars, and image upscaling at 1080p/2K/4K by tier. Flow also routes to Gemini Omni ('create and edit videos from any input reference — real or generated') and Nano Banana for images. This is the clearest example in the category of a foundation-model vendor eating the application layer.

Key features ·  Veo 3.1 Standard / Fast / Lite tiers, audio included by default on all · 4K output on Standard ($0.60/s) and Fast ($0.30/s) · Flow Scenebuilder, camera controls, Ingredients-to-Video, video extension · Natural-language video-to-video editing · Characters & Avatars for cross-shot consistency · Upscaling to 1080p / 2K / 4K · Gemini Omni multimodal model inside Flow · Charged only on successful generation
Pricing Veo 3.1 Standard $0.40/s (720p, 1080p), $0.60/s (4K). Fast $0.10/s (720p), $0.12/s (1080p), $0.30/s (4K). Lite $0.05/s (720p), $0.08/s (1080p). Veo 3 Standard $0.40/s; Veo 2 $0.35/s. Flow plans: Free (50 daily credits), Google AI Plus $4.99/mo (200 credits), AI Pro $19.99/mo (1,000), AI Ultra $99.99-$199.99/mo (10,000-25,000).
Scale & ownership Google/DeepMind. Distribution through Google AI subscription tiers and the Gemini API. Specific user counts not disclosed.

Lightricks LTX-2.5 / LTX-2 (open weights) + LTX Studio huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5 DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
The single most consequential entry for Cinamate: a 22B open-weight audio-video model you self-host with no per-generation billing, from a vendor that also ships its own storyboard-to-film studio app.

LTX-2.5 is a 22B-parameter audio-video generative model with open weights on Hugging Face, distributed as components totalling roughly 66 GiB, in distilled and full/dev variants. It includes a dedicated audio VAE for native synchronized audio and a duration head that predicts clip length from the prompt. Inference supports fp8 casting and CPU/disk offload for constrained VRAM. The earlier LTXV 0.9.8 line (13B dev, 2B distilled, OpenRail-M) supported up to 60 seconds at 1216x704/30fps, with a 2B distilled LoRA variant claimed to run in 1GB of VRAM and HD generation in ~10 seconds on an H100. Lightricks separately operates LTX Studio, an application-layer product for storyboard-driven production.

Key features ·  22B open-weight audio-video model, downloadable checkpoints · Native synchronized audio generation with a separate audio VAE · Duration head — automatic length prediction from prompt · fp8-cast quantization and --offload cpu/disk for low-VRAM machines · Distilled variants for speed; prior 2B distilled LoRA claimed at 1GB VRAM · Prior LTXV 0.9.8 supported up to 60-second videos · Self-host: 'no per-generation billing, no per-seat lock-in' · LTX Studio app layer sits above the model
Pricing Weights are free to download. LTX-2.x Community License Agreement: entities with annual revenues of at least $10,000,000 are 'required to obtain a paid license for any use' other than testing/evaluation/non-commercial R&D. Below that threshold, commercial use is free. Prior LTXV 0.9.5+ used OpenRail-M. Hosted LTX-2.5 pro/fast variants are sold on fal.ai; those per-second rates were not confirmed in this pass. LTX Studio plan pricing not retrievable (page did not render).
Scale & ownership Lightricks (also Facetune, Videoleap). Funding not verified in this pass. LTX-Video is one of the most-adopted open video model families, integrated in ComfyUI and diffusers.
Collides with ·  Studio / Local Generation (this is plausibly the engine class Cinamate depends on) · Cinamate's entire $0.00-cloud / ~$110-per-feature economic claim · boards and writer (via LTX Studio's storyboard-driven app layer) · The Cutting Room (LTX Studio assembly)

  • Native synchronized audio in the open weights

OpenAI Sora 2 / Sora 2 Pro developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
OpenAI's flagship video+audio generation model, sold via API and a consumer Sora app, and still the reference point every other vendor is benchmarked against.

Sora 2 and Sora 2 Pro generate video with synchronized audio from text or a first-frame image. The API supports 16- and 20-second generations, reusable character assets for consistency across shots, an edits endpoint (the older remix endpoint is deprecated), and downloadable spritesheets. Sora 2 covers 480p/720p; Sora 2 Pro adds 1024p and true 1080p at 1920x1080 or 1080x1920. As of this pass there is no Sora 3 — the developer model catalog lists no video model beyond sora-2 and sora-2-pro.

Key features ·  Text-to-video and image-to-video with native synchronized audio · 16s and 20s generation lengths · 1080p exports on Sora 2 Pro (1920x1080 / 1080x1920) · Reusable character assets for cross-shot consistency (best at 2-4s, 720p-1080p) · Edits endpoint for iterative revision · 50% batch discount for non-interactive jobs · Consumer Sora app driving mass distribution
Pricing API per second of output. sora-2 720p $0.10/s. sora-2-pro $0.30/s (720p), $0.50/s (1024p), $0.70/s (1080p). Batch tier is half: sora-2 720p $0.05/s; sora-2-pro $0.15/$0.25/$0.35 per second. Consumer app pricing not verified in this pass.
Scale & ownership OpenAI; funding and valuation not verified in this pass. The Sora consumer app gives it consumer-scale distribution no other video model has.

Runway (Gen-4.5, Aleph 2.0, Edit Studio) runway.com/pricing DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
The most production-oriented of the model vendors — it now ships an editing studio, node-based workflows, an autonomous agent, and professional delivery formats Cinamate does not support.

Runway sells Gen-4.5 and Gen-4 Turbo generation plus Aleph 2.0 & Edit Studio for video-to-video editing ('edit a frame in a video, apply it to the rest'). It has custom node-based workflows chaining multiple models and intermediary steps, real-time conversational Characters agents, a Runway Agent that creates end-to-end videos from conversation, and Runway MCP to connect Claude/ChatGPT to its tools. It resells ByteDance Seedance 2 and 2.5 through the same API with a Model Router. Use-case apps include Remove from Video, Upscale Video, Add Dialogue, Relight Scene, Change Time of Day, Reshoot Product.

Key features ·  Gen-4.5 and Gen-4 Turbo generation models · Aleph 2.0 & Edit Studio — propagated video-to-video editing · Node-based multi-model workflow builder · Runway Agent for end-to-end video from conversation · Runway MCP integration with external AI assistants · Model Router (bills at the selected model's rate, disclosed in response metadata) · ProRes and PNG sequence delivery, and HDR profiles · Resells Seedance 2 / 2.5 alongside its own models

ByteDance Seedance (1.0 / 2.0 / 2.5) seed.bytedance.com/en/seedance DIRECT HIGH VERIFIED
ByteDance's video model line, notable for native multi-shot narrative generation and a 30-second single-shot capability that attacks the storyboard-to-scene workflow directly.

Seedance 1.0 generates 1080p video with 'smooth motion, rich details, and cinematic aesthetics' from text and images, and — most importantly — 'natively supports the generation of narrative videos with multiple cohesive shots.' Luma AI — Ray3.2 / Ray3.14 (Dream Machine) lumalabs.ai/pricing DIRECT HIGH VERIFIED
The only model vendor verified to sell HDR and EXR output, making it the most post-production-literate generation product in the category.

Luma's current Ray line comprises Ray3.2 and Ray3.14, sold on a per-second credit basis with tiered resolutions from Draft through 1080p. Uniquely, Luma prices HDR and EXR as explicit output multipliers — Ray3.2 offers SDR base, HDR at 2x, and HDR+EXR at 3x; Ray3.14 offers SDR base and HDR at 4x. EXR is a linear-light compositing format used in professional VFX pipelines, and no other vendor surveyed advertises it. Ray3.14 also appears as a free-tier partner model inside Adobe Firefly.

Ray3.14 credits per second: Draft 4, 540p 10, 720p 20, 1080p 80. Ray3.2 per 5 seconds: Draft 20, 540p 50, 720p 100, 1080p 400 (same per-second rates). HDR/EXR multipliers as above. Adobe Firefly www.adobe.com/products/firefly/plans.html ADJACENT HIGH VERIFIED
The incumbent's aggregation play — 30+ AI models including Veo, Kling, Runway and Luma inside the company that already owns Premiere Pro and After Effects.

Firefly bundles Adobe's own Firefly Video Model with third-party partner models — Veo 3.1 Fast, Kling 3.0, Runway, Luma Ray3.14, Nano Banana — under one subscription and one generative-credit pool, positioning itself to 'Generate images, video, audio and more with 30+ AI models, all in one place.' All paid tiers generate 5-second videos, with volume rising by tier and the top tier granting unlimited access to the Firefly Video Model. The strategic weight here is not the model quality — it is that Adobe owns the NLE that Cinamate's Cutting Room is trying to replace, and is now routing generation into that same account.

Alibaba Wan (Wan 2.2 open / Wan 2.5 closed) github.com/Wan-Video/Wan2.2 ADJACENT HIGH VERIFIED
The most permissively licensed serious open video model family — Apache 2.0 through 2.2 — but Alibaba has stopped open-sourcing the newest tier, which is the category's warning shot.

Wan2.2 (released 28 July 2025, Apache 2.0) ships several variants: T2V-A14B and I2V-A14B are 27B-parameter MoE models with 14B active per step requiring at least 80GB VRAM; TI2V-5B is a 5B model needing 'at least 24GB VRAM (e.g, RTX 4090)' and generating 5-second 720P video at 1280x704; S2V-14B is an audio-driven cinematic video model whose length auto-adjusts to input audio, with TTS via CosyVoice; Animate-14B handles character animation. The org also maintains Wan-Dancer, Wan-Animate-2, and a Wan-skills agent repo. Critically, the Wan-Video GitHub organization contains no Wan2.5 or Wan3 repository — Wan 2.5 is sold as a hosted model on fal.ai at $0.05/second with no corresponding open weights.

Pricing Wan 2.2 and earlier: weights free under Apache 2.0. Wan 2.5 hosted on fal.ai at $0.05 per second. Wan 2.1 on Replicate via wavespeedai: $0.09/second (i2v-480p), $0.25/second (i2v-720p). Alibaba Cloud Model Studio pricing page returned 503 in this pass.

ComfyUI / Comfy Cloud www.comfy.org/pricing ADJACENT HIGH VERIFIED
The free, open-source local inference runtime that is the de facto standard for running open-weight video models on your own GPU — and therefore the default alternative to Cinamate's Local Generation.

ComfyUI is a node-graph runtime for local generative model inference, distributed as a free desktop download. It is the standard host for LTX-Video, Wan, HunyuanVideo, Mochi and most open video weights, and it materially lowers their VRAM requirements (it is credited with running Mochi under 20GB against a ~60GB baseline). Comfy Cloud offers hosted execution on subscription tiers, and Partner Nodes route proprietary models through the same credit pool. Moonvalley distributes Marey through it.

Key features ·  Free open-source local desktop runtime · Node-graph workflow authoring for arbitrary model chains · VRAM optimization that makes large models fit consumer cards · Hosted Comfy Cloud tiers with a shared credit pool · Partner Nodes for proprietary models (e.g. Nano Banana Pro) on the same credits · Ecosystem hub — most open video weights ship ComfyUI support first
Pricing Desktop app free/open-source. Comfy Cloud month-to-month: Standard $20, Creator $35, Pro $100, Team $700 (annual-billing equivalents $16/$28/$80/$630; credits 4,200/7,400/21,100/147,700). [vendor-verified]
Scale & ownership Comfy Org. Funding not verified in this pass. Effectively the standard local runtime for open-weight generative video; ecosystem-wide adoption.

MiniMax H3 / Hailuo github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3 ADJACENT HIGH VERIFIED
An open-weight 33B omni-modal generation model with native stereo audio — currently live as Hailuo's flagship and among the most capable weights you can actually download.

MiniMax-H3 is a general-purpose multimodal generative system with 'unified understanding of multimodal contexts composed of text, images, video, and audio.' The H3-Omni-Transformer is approximately 33B parameters (roughly 13B in AdaLN-related branches). It generates video with native stereo audio, supporting text-to-video, first/last-frame-to-video, and multimodal reference-based generation, at 4-15 seconds and 24 FPS, 768p base with 2K via a Regenerate module, across a wide range of aspect ratios. Open checkpoints cover H3-Base in FL2VA and Ref2VA variants — but H3-Context-IR and H3-Regenerate-2K are explicitly not open-sourced. The repo was updated 15 August 2026 and MiniMax's own site describes H3 as 'an open-weight, general-purpose, omni-modal generation model'; hailuoai.video shows 'MiniMax H3 LIVE NOW'.

Key features ·  ~33B parameter omni-modal transformer, open base checkpoints · Native stereo audio with generated video · 4-15 second durations at 24 FPS — longer than most open models · 768p base, 2K via H3-Regenerate-2K (closed) · Text-to-video, first/last-frame-to-video, reference-based generation · MiniMax H3 Community License, weights on Hugging Face · Hailuo 02 legacy tier available cheaply on fal.ai · Repo actively updated as of August 2026
Pricing H3 weights free to download under the MiniMax H3 Community License. Hosted Hailuo 02 on fal.ai: $0.045/second, or $0.27 per 6-second video, at 768p. MiniMax's own price page did not disclose per-model video rates; platform.minimax.io/docs/price returned 404.
Scale & ownership MiniMax (China). MiniMax-H3 repo shows 6,809 stars; the org also ships MiniMax-Music3, a CLI, an MCP server and a 13.4k-star skills repo. Funding and valuation not verified in this pass.

Tencent HunyuanVideo 1.5 github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanVideo-1.5 ADJACENT HIGH VERIFIED
The most consumer-GPU-friendly credible open-weight video model — 8.3B parameters running in 14GB of VRAM on an RTX 4090.

HunyuanVideo-1.5, released 21 November 2025, is an 8.3B-parameter open-weight video model explicitly engineered for accessibility: a 14GB minimum GPU memory footprint that 'runs smoothly on consumer-grade GPUs, making it accessible for every developer.' It outputs 480p and 720p at up to 121 frames (~5s at 24fps). A step-distilled variant delivers a claimed 75% speedup, generating a video 'within 75 seconds' on a single RTX 4090; standard inference is roughly 2-3 minutes on high-end hardware. The original HunyuanVideo was 13B parameters and needed 60GB for 720p — the 1.5 release is a deliberate order-of-magnitude accessibility move.

Moonvalley Marey www.moonvalley.com DIRECT MEDIUM VERIFIED
The clean-rights, filmmaker-first model — trained exclusively on licensed footage and sold on the commercial-safety argument that Cinamate's clearance and contracts modules imply matters.

Marey is Moonvalley's image-to-video and text-to-video model, explicitly positioned as 'Fully Licensed, Commercially safe' and 'Trained on licensed data' and 'high-resolution cinematic footage.' The feature set is unusually production-literate: Pose Transfer (motion guidance from reference inputs), Camera Control (cinematic camera moves from a single image), Motion Transfer, Trajectory Control (draw object paths without prompting), Advanced Lighting (studio-grade lighting with natural shadows), plus prompt adherence and natural physics. Moonvalley describes itself as 'a research lab focused on pushing the frontiers of creativity through deep learning.' Marey launched publicly on 8 July 2025, with inference partnerships via ComfyUI and fal.ai. The site references 'Marey Realism v1.5.'

fal.ai fal.ai/pricing INDIRECT MEDIUM VERIFIED
The inference marketplace where nearly every video model is resold at a published per-second price — effectively the public price index that Cinamate's cost claims will be measured against.

fal.ai describes itself as 'The Fastest Generative AI Platform for Developers,' hosting models from Google, OpenAI, xAI, Alibaba, ByteDance, ElevenLabs and Black Forest Labs behind one API with transparent per-second or per-video pricing. Its video catalogue currently spans Seedance 2.5, Gemini Omni, Kling 3.0, Veo 3.1, MiniMax H3, Wan, LTX-2.5 (pro and fast), Grok Imagine 1.5 Video and Hailuo. For a product like Cinamate, fal is simultaneously the easiest way to add cloud fallback for users without a local GPU, and the benchmark that makes any inflated 'savings' claim checkable in thirty seconds.

A 10B Apache-2.0 open video model that was significant in late 2024 and has been effectively dormant since — a cautionary example of open-weight roadmap risk.

Mochi 1 is a 10B-parameter diffusion video model released under Apache 2.0, generating 480p video. It requires roughly 60GB VRAM on a single GPU, though ComfyUI optimization brings it under 20GB. Native ComfyUI support landed 5 November 2024 and LoRA fine-tuning support 26 November 2024. Despite 63 commits on main and open issues, no substantive model release has followed, leaving it two generations behind the current open frontier.

NVIDIA's open-weight world foundation models — aimed at robotics and autonomous vehicles rather than filmmaking, and already deprecated in favour of Cosmos 3.

Cosmos-Predict2.5, released 6 October 2025, comes in 2B and 14B parameter variants and 'unifies Text2World, Image2World, and Video2World into a single model' for predicting future video states from multimodal inputs. Weights are distributed on Hugging Face under the NVIDIA Open Model License (source code is Apache 2.0), so it is open-weight but not OSI open-source. The stated target is 'physical AI applications such as autonomous vehicles (AVs), robots, and video analytics AI agents,' with specialized autonomous-driving and robotics variants. The repository notes it is deprecated in favour of Cosmos 3, with 'only limited maintenance updates' going forward.

Open-Sora (HPC-AI Tech) github.com/hpcaitech/Open-Sora INDIRECT LOW VERIFIED
An 11B Apache-2.0 open video model notable mainly for its $200k training-cost claim — but its repo last pushed April 2026, leaving it well behind the current open frontier.

Open-Sora 2.0, released 12 March 2025 under Apache-2.0, is an 11B-parameter video generation model (earlier versions were 1B and 3B). It supports 256px and 768px resolution with frame counts of 4k+1 under 129, across 16:9, 9:16, 1:1 and 2.39:1 aspect ratios. VRAM is substantial: 44.3-60.3GB peak across 8 GPUs for 768x768, and roughly 52.5GB for single-GPU inference at 256x256. The project's headline claim is 'Training a Commercial-Level Video Generation Model in $200k.' The repo shows 1,333 commits with ongoing VAE and transformer refinements, but no release newer than 2.0 was found.

Zhipu / Z.ai CogVideoX github.com/zai-org/CogVideo INDIRECT LOW VERIFIED
An early open-weight video model whose real distinction is the lowest VRAM floor in the category — 7GB quantized — but it has not shipped a new model since November 2024.

CogVideoX1.5-5B, released 8 November 2024, is a 5B-parameter open video model generating 5- or 10-second clips at 1360x768, with frame counts following a 16N+1 rule where N is at most 10. Its notable property is accessibility: Diffusers BF16 runs from 10GB VRAM and INT8 quantized from 7GB, making it viable on an RTX 3060. Speed is the tradeoff — roughly 1,000 seconds on a single A100 at 50 steps for a 5-second video, about half that on an H100. CogVideoX-5B uses the bespoke CogVideoX LICENSE while CogVideoX-2B is Apache 2.0. Last repo update was the CogKit fine-tuning framework in March 2025.

§16 AI voice, ADR, dubbing, music & sound ⟦S16⟧

Market read · This category has already had its reckoning, and Cinamate has not. Three things define it in August 2026. First, consolidation at the top: ElevenLabs raised $500M at an $11B valuation in February 2026 and is the default voice layer, while Respeecher (~$3M raised) survives on film credits and Replica Studios — the first AI voice company to sign with SAG-AFTRA — simply shut down. Second, provenance became the product. Flawless holds TPN Gold, SOC 2, ISO 27001 and MPA compliance and built A.R.T., a contractual actor-consent gate, in collaboration with SAG-AFTRA and the DGA. Deepdub is TPN and SOC 2 certified with a licensed voice library and artist royalties. Adobe, Stability, Soundraw and Beatoven all lead with training-data provenance; Beatoven and Voice-Swap carry Fairly Trained certification; Resemble pivoted to selling deepfake detection and EU AI Act watermarking. Third, the music side has been settled by litigation: Suno paid Warner $500M and licensed BMG, Udio settled with Universal and relaunched licensed-only after giving users 48 hours to download their work. Pricing has bifurcated — self-serve at $6-$50/month, enterprise unpriced. The implication for Cinamate is sharp. Its music/cue-sheet room collides with an entrenched incumbent (Music Reports processes over a million cue sheets a year for Netflix, HBO and Apple), and its generated-voice elements land in a market where certification, union agreements and documented consent are now table stakes. Cinamate's disclosed lack of TPN, SOC 2, a public team or press coverage is not a cosmetic gap here — it is the exact axis on which this category now competes. Note also that ElevenLabs' self-serve music licence explicitly excludes film and TV, and that F5-TTS and AudioCraft ship non-commercial weights: a local-GPU render pipeline can silently produce an undeliverable film.
ElevenLabs elevenlabs.io DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
The default AI voice layer for the industry — TTS, voice cloning, 90+ language dubbing and licensed AI music — now a $11B company.

ElevenLabs is the category's centre of gravity for generated speech. Dubbing v2 covers 90+ languages with an audio-to-audio model that conditions on the source performance rather than a transcript, doing sync-aware translation and automatic voice cloning that preserves speaker identity. The Voice Library holds 11,000+ voices plus an Iconic Voices Marketplace with formally licensed estates and characters (Sir Michael Caine, Stan Lee, Judy Garland, John Wayne, Dr. Maya Angelou, Sir Laurence Olivier, Megatron, Optimus Prime). ElevenProductions is a managed service layering human translators, voice casting and professional mixing on top for studios and broadcasters; Eleven Music v2 generates songs the company says are trained on licensed data only.

Flawless www.flawlessai.com ADJACENT CRITICAL VERIFIED
Visual dubbing and in-vision ADR for major studios — and the company that already holds every certification Cinamate is missing.

Flawless builds what it calls assistive (not generative) AI for film and television, deliberately positioning against generative tools. DeepEditor syncs new or adjusted dialogue to existing footage, enabling in-vision ADR, performance transfer between takes, censorship editing and pacing changes without a reshoot. Open-source audio stack (F5-TTS, AudioCraft/MusicGen, Stable Audio Open) github.com/SWivid/F5-TTS INDIRECT MEDIUM VERIFIED
Free local-GPU voice and music models that undercut every paid vendor — but most ship non-commercial weights, which is a delivery trap for films.

The open-source stack is the substitute a local-GPU product like Cinamate is most likely to be built on and most likely to be replaced by. F5-TTS ('A Fairytaler that Fakes Fluent and Faithful Speech with Flow Matching') does zero-shot voice cloning with multi-style and multi-speaker generation. Meta's AudioCraft bundles MusicGen (text-and-melody-conditioned music), AudioGen (text-to-sound-effects), EnCodec, MAGNeT, AudioSeal watermarking, MusicGen Style and JASCO. Stability's Stable Audio Small and Medium ship open weights. The critical and widely misunderstood detail is the licence split: F5-TTS code is MIT but its pretrained models are CC-BY-NC because they were trained on Emilia; AudioCraft code is MIT but its model weights are CC-BY-NC 4.0. Both explicitly prohibit commercial use of the weights.

Key features ·  F5-TTS — zero-shot cloning, diffusion transformer + ConvNeXt V2, multi-style/multi-speaker, 15.2k stars · MusicGen — text and melody-conditioned music generation · AudioGen — text-to-sound-effects generation · AudioSeal — open watermarking for generated audio · MAGNeT, JASCO (chord/melody/drum conditioning), MusicGen Style · Stable Audio Small and Medium with downloadable open weights · AudioCraft: 23.6k stars, 2.7k forks
Pricing Free. Cost is GPU time and engineering only.
Scale & ownership F5-TTS 15.2k GitHub stars / 2.2k forks. AudioCraft 23.6k stars / 2.7k forks. Meta and Stability AI as institutional backers of the respective releases.
Collides with ·  Studio/Local Generation — the direct substitute for Cinamate's generated-voice and generated-score elements · music/cue sheets room (MusicGen, AudioGen, Stable Audio Open) · post (sound design) · The Money Room's price-per-render pitch (open source renders at zero marginal licence cost)
Stronger than Cinamate
  • Free and self-hosted — the strongest possible answer to Cinamate's '$0.00 cloud billing' argument
  • Runs on the same local GPU Cinamate already requires, with no vendor at all
  • AudioSeal provides open watermarking; Cinamate offers no provenance marking
  • No invite gate, no beta, no vendor dependency or shutdown risk
  • Full auditability of what the model is and how it is licensed
Weaker than Cinamate
  • The licensing trap is severe: F5-TTS and AudioCraft pretrained weights are CC-BY-NC — non-commercial only. Any film delivered with them has a defective chain of title unless the weights are relicensed or retrained
  • No consent mechanism, no talent licensing, no royalty path — a direct union and likeness risk
  • No product, no UI, no support; requires real ML engineering
  • No cue sheets, no rights administration, no production management
  • Quality and consistency below the commercial leaders for narrative dialogue

Udio www.udio.com INDIRECT MEDIUM VERIFIED
Ex-DeepMind music generator that settled with Universal and relaunched licensed-only — after giving users 48 hours to download their catalogue.

Udio generates music with vocals and instrumentation from text prompts specifying genre, lyrics and style. Founded in December 2023 as Uncharted Labs by four former Google DeepMind researchers, it went viral in 2024 with the 'BBL Drizzy' parody. The RIAA sued it alongside Suno in June 2024. In October 2025 it reached a licensing settlement with Universal Music Group and agreed to launch a platform trained only on authorized and licensed music — a total business-model reset. Existing users were given 48 hours to download their creations before the platform moved to a streaming-based system.

Key features ·  Text-prompt music generation with vocals and instrumentation · Extendable track generation from initial 30-second segments · Post-settlement: trained only on authorized and licensed music · Streaming-based delivery model replacing free downloading

§17 Editorial, post-production, review & VFX/asset tracking ⟦S17⟧

Market read · Structure: this category has consolidated into four platform owners and two roll-ups. Adobe holds Premiere Pro + Frame.io + Firefly; Blackmagic holds Resolve + Blackmagic Cloud + cameras; Autodesk has assembled the entire dailies-to-VFX-tracking chain under Flow (Flow Production Tracking/ShotGrid, Flow Capture/Moxion, and now PIX — pixsystem.com redirects to autodesk.com); Backlight (founded 2021) has rolled up iconik, ftrack, cineSync, Celtx, Wildmoka and Zype; EditShare owns EFS/FLOW/FLEX plus MediaSilo, Screeners and Wiredrive. Independents survive at the edges: Colorfront and Codex on dailies/mastering, Pomfort on set, Sohonet and Evercast on real-time review, Foundry on compositing, Kitsu and AYON as open-source trackers. Pricing norms: editorial is nearly free ($0 Resolve, $295 Resolve Studio perpetual, $22.99/mo Premiere). Review and tracking sit at $9–$65 per seat (Frame.io $15–$25, MediaSilo $15–$25, iconik $9–$120, Kitsu €20–€35, AYON €19–€38). Only compositing ($3,839–$6,379/yr Nuke) and secure enterprise dailies (PIX, Colorfront, Sohonet, Evercast — all quote-only) are expensive. What this means for Cinamate: every AI feature The Cutting Room advertises — rough cut, silence trim, music sync, colour balance — ships today inside Premiere (Remix, Color Match, text-based editing), Resolve 21's Neural Engine, Descript's Underlord, CuttingRoom's Shortcut, Kapwing's Smart Cut. None of it is defensible. Two structural gaps are worse than the feature parity problem: Cinamate claims EDL/OTIO but not AAF, and AAF is the handoff format every finishing house, audio post and Avid cutting room expects — without it the master cannot leave the building professionally. And no TPN or SOC 2, on a netlify.app subdomain, is disqualifying under any studio or distributor security addendum, which is precisely where Evercast, PIX and Frame.io Enterprise compete. Cinamate's only real edge here is that all 28 rooms share one state; no competitor above does that, but a 4-minute sync, single-operator design, no camera ingest and no NLE plugin means it wins only where the operator is the entire post department.
Adobe Premiere Pro (with Firefly Generative Extend) www.adobe.com/products/premiere.html DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
The dominant professional NLE, now shipping the exact AI edit-assist feature set Cinamate markets as novel.

Desktop non-linear editor for film, TV and streaming, bundled into Creative Cloud alongside After Effects, Audition and Frame.io. The current release adds Firefly-powered Generative Extend (extends clips and generates missing ambient sound), AI Object Mask, Media Intelligence search (find footage by describing audio or dialogue), text-based editing with automatic transcription in 18 languages, Color Match, Enhance Speech, AI audio category tagging, and Remix (AI music retiming to picture). Frame.io review is integrated directly into the timeline. Round-trips AAF, EDL, XML and OTIO to and from Avid, Resolve and finishing houses.

Key features ·  Generative Extend (Adobe Firefly) for clip extension and generated ambient audio · AI Object Mask with automatic subject tracking · Media Intelligence search by described audio or spoken dialogue · Text-based editing / automatic transcription in 18 languages · Color Match (AI shot matching) and Enhance Speech · Remix — AI music retiming to cut length · Native Frame.io panel for review and C2C media · AAF / EDL / XML / OTIO interchange

§18 Storyboards, animatics, previs & concept ⟦S18⟧

Market read · Research caveat: the WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted before I began, so this category was built almost entirely from direct page fetches. Most entries are verified from live product and pricing pages; where a page was blocked (Blender, Unreal, FrameForge, StudioBinder, LTX Studio pricing) I have said so and lowered confidence rather than guessing figures. The category splits three ways. First, the craft incumbents: Toon Boom Storyboard Pro ($87/mo, $752/yr, v27) owns professional animation boarding, with FrameForge, Shot Designer (free, €19.99 Pro) and Previs Pro serving directors and DPs who need geometrically truthful blocking. Second, the collaboration layer: Boords ($39-$250/mo), StudioBinder, Krock ($10/user/mo) and MakeStoryboard compete on review, versioning and client sign-off, not on picture-making. Third, the 2025-26 AI wave: Katalist ($19-$99/mo), StoryboardHero ($19-$199/mo), LTX Studio and FinalBit AI (the rebranded Nolan AI) all promise script-to-board-to-video. Direction of travel is unambiguous. Pricing is collapsing toward $10-$40/month for AI boards, and AI generation is becoming a feature of existing products (Boords, Krock, StudioBinder-adjacent) rather than a product category. Model supply is commoditising: Katalist simply resells Runway, Veo, Kling, Sora and LTX-2. Attrition is real — Cine Tracer's domain is gone, Storyboarder's last release is a February 2024 pre-release, Lore Machine's domain now belongs to a defence-AI firm, and Plot does not resolve. For Cinamate the danger is precise. Its boards room is one of 28 modules, so per-feature it will lose to Boords and Storyboard Pro. Its real moat is the spine — Money Room, tax credits, union rates, breakeven modelling — that nobody here touches. But Lightricks giving away free, open-source, locally-run generation via LTX Desktop attacks the "local GPU, $0.00 cloud billing" story head-on, and Previs Pro's iOS app plus NLE export hits Cinamate's two admitted gaps at $359.99 lifetime. Cinamate should stop selling boards and start selling the spine.
Boords boords.com DIRECT HIGH VERIFIED
The category-leading dedicated script-to-storyboard-to-animatic tool with a client review and sign-off workflow.

Boords is a browser-based pre-production platform that takes a script, breaks it into storyboard frames with camera angles and shot descriptions, generates or sources the frame art, and turns the board into a timed animatic in one click. Its AI generator offers sketch, vector-illustration and photorealistic styles and keeps a reusable cast consistent across frames. The differentiating layer is approval: clients review and comment frame-by-frame via a link with no signup, and every version, comment and sign-off is tracked. Founded 2015 by James Chambers (previously co-founder of animation studio Animade); still independent.

Key features ·  AI storyboard generation in 3 styles with reusable, consistent characters · Script-to-shot-list with camera angles and frame compositions · One-click animatic editor · No-signup client review, frame-level commenting, password-protected share links · Version control and activity trail / sign-off audit · 3M+ integrated stock image library · PDF and multi-format export · 2FA, project-level permissions, SSO (SAML) on Enterprise
Pricing Published: Solo $39/mo (1 user, 250 AI images/mo); Pro $75/mo (5 users, 1,000 AI images); Team $125/mo (10 users, 2,000); Agency $250/mo (30 users, 3,000); Enterprise custom. Yearly billing ~33% cheaper (~$26/$50/$85/$165 per month equivalent).
Scale & ownership Founded 2015, independent, bootstrapped-appearing. Site claims 1M+ creative projects shared for review and 12M+ comments captured. Named customers include Framestore, Partizan and Vidico.

Katalist www.katalist.ai DIRECT HIGH VERIFIED
Script-to-storyboard-to-video AI studio with consistent characters and a Premiere Pro integration, priced aggressively at $19-$99/month.

Katalist converts a script into a storyboard with consistent character appearance across frames, then generates video from those shots. It aggregates the leading third-party video models (Runway Gen-4, Google Veo 3.2, Kling, Pixverse, Sora 2, LTX-2) rather than running its own, and adds lip-sync, AI voiceover and an AI script assistant. Its commercial centre of gravity has shifted toward performance advertising — a 'Product Swap Engine' replaces products in existing videos from real product photography to scale across SKUs without reshoots.

Previs Pro www.previspro.com DIRECT HIGH VERIFIED
3D previs and animatics on Mac, iPad and iPhone with LiDAR location scanning, AR virtual camera and NLE timeline export — and a $359.99 lifetime licence.

Previs Pro ('See it before you shoot it') builds 3D scenes with customisable props, characters, lighting and cameras, then captures camera and actor movement into animatics. It imports Final Draft, Fountain, Celtx and Open Format screenplays, scans real locations with LiDAR, and offers an AR virtual camera to place a virtual scene into a real space on an iPhone or iPad. It exports storyboards, animatics, MP4s and NLE timelines to Premiere, DaVinci Resolve and Final Cut, with directors' markup tools and photorealistic or sketch rendering. AI generation of props and actors from text descriptions is built in.

The free, open-source desktop storyboarding app with a 3D Shot Generator and VR — beloved, widely used, and effectively stalled since 2024.

Storyboarder is a free, open-source drawing-first boarding application for macOS, Windows and Linux. It offers six drawing instruments, onion skin, guides and reference layers, and a 'Shot Generator' that builds a 3D reference shot from a typed description so a director can block a frame without drawing it. Krock.io krock.io ADJACENT MEDIUM VERIFIED
Review-and-approval platform for animation and video teams with a free storyboard creator, AI storyboarding and animatic export, priced at a flat $10/user/month.

Krock.io is a creative collaboration platform centred on review and approval of video, image, audio and PDF with time-coded commenting, version control, and calendar/Gantt project views. Layered on top is a storyboard toolset — a free storyboard creator, an interactive 'Board' for planning projects, scripts, storyboards and animatics, and 'Storyboard AI' for AI-powered storyboarding. Its commercial hook is that reviewers and collaborators are unlimited and free on every plan, with no per-user fees for people who only comment.

Key features ·  Free storyboard creator plus animatic export · Storyboard AI for AI-generated boards · Time-coded review and approval on video, image, audio and PDF · Unlimited free reviewers on every plan · Version control, workspaces, calendar and Gantt views · 4K playback and custom branding on Pro · Integrations with DaVinci Resolve, Adobe Creative Cloud and Final Cut Pro
Pricing Published: Free $0 (1 user, 2GB, 1 workspace, 2 projects, 50 AI tokens, storyboard tool, unlimited reviewers); Pro $10/user/mo (unlimited projects and workspaces, from 2TB storage, +1TB add-on at $10/mo, 4K playback, custom branding); Enterprise/Unlimited from $400 with 100 users included and unlimited collaborators.
Scale & ownership Funding and headquarters not disclosed on the pages reviewed. Case-study customers named: Krafton Americas, Hound, Animade, PE (Passion Entertainment).

Blender (Grease Pencil / Video Sequence Editor previs pipeline) www.blender.org INDIRECT MEDIUM LIKELY
The free open-source 3D suite that a large share of indie and animation previs actually runs on, at zero licence cost.

Blender is a free, open-source 3D creation suite whose Grease Pencil 2D-in-3D drawing system and built-in Video Sequence Editor let teams board, block and cut animatics entirely inside one free application. The 'storypencil' workflow links a 2D drawing scene to a 3D layout scene so boards and camera blocking stay in sync. For animation studios and indie live-action teams alike it is the zero-cost substitute for both a boarding tool and a previs package. Note: blender.org returned 403 to automated fetching during this research, so version and licence specifics here rest on background knowledge rather than a page I loaded.

Key features ·  Grease Pencil for drawing 2D boards inside 3D space · Storypencil workflow linking board scenes to 3D layout · Built-in Video Sequence Editor for cutting animatics · Full 3D previs: cameras, lenses, lighting, layout, simulation · Python scripting and a very large add-on ecosystem · Runs locally on the user's own GPU, cross-platform · Free with no seat cost at any scale
Pricing Free. Open-source under the GNU GPL; no licence fee at any studio size. (Licence terms not verified from a loaded page in this research.)

Unreal Engine previs / virtual production pipeline (Epic Games) www.unrealengine.com INDIRECT MEDIUM UNCERTAIN
The engine underneath essentially all high-end professional previs and virtual production, free to use for film and TV linear content.

Unreal Engine is the realtime engine that professional previs houses and virtual production stages are built on. Sequencer provides a cinematic timeline, virtual camera and Live Link systems let a director hand-hold a virtual camera on a volume or in a room, and the engine drives LED-wall in-camera VFX. For linear content — film, TV and broadcast — Epic's licensing has historically been free of the game-revenue royalty, which is why the entire high-end previs sector standardised on it. Note: unrealengine.com returned 403 to automated fetching during this research, so the specific 2025-26 seat-fee and revenue-threshold terms could not be confirmed and should be checked directly.

Key features ·  Sequencer cinematic timeline for previs and techvis · Virtual camera and Live Link for realtime camera capture · In-camera VFX / LED volume driving · Photoreal realtime rendering with full lens and lighting control · Massive asset marketplace and studio-grade pipeline tooling · Runs on local hardware at any scale
Pricing Not verified in this research. Epic's licensing for non-game linear content has historically carried no game-style royalty, with per-seat terms introduced for some non-game commercial use; exact 2025-26 seat fees and revenue thresholds could not be loaded and should be treated as unverified.
Scale & ownership Epic Games — one of the largest private software companies in the world. The de facto engine of the professional previs and virtual production industry. Specific seat counts and film-sector revenue not disclosed.

Cine Tracer store.steampowered.com DIRECT LOW VERIFIED
Unreal-Engine-based realtime cinematography simulator sold on Steam at $89.99 — and its own website domain has now been lost to an unrelated business.

Cine Tracer is a realtime cinematography and previs simulator built on Unreal Engine and distributed through Steam, letting a DP or director block shots with physically-modelled cameras, lenses and lighting in a game-engine environment. It was an early and influential proof that game engines could serve as an indie previs tool. Its status in 2026 is the story: it remains listed and purchasable on Steam at $89.99 with a 28 September 2018 release date, but cinetracer.com now 301-redirects to providenceplace-apartments.com — the product domain has been let go or sold, a strong signal that active development and marketing have ceased.

Key features ·  Realtime cinematography simulation on Unreal Engine · Physically-modelled cameras, lenses and lighting · Shot blocking and previs in a game-engine environment · Distributed and updated through Steam

ShotPro www.shotprofessional.com DIRECT LOW VERIFIED
Cross-platform 3D storyboard and previs app with 1D/2D/3D modes and pro camera controls, but showing signs of neglect.

ShotPro is a visualisation and previs application for iOS, iPad, Mac and Windows that builds 3D storyboards and animated scenes. It structures work in three modes: 1D for scripts, scenes and shot lists; 2D for fast blocking of character, camera and prop movement; and 3D for final polish. 'Pro Cam' exposes aperture, focus distance, ISO, shutter speed, lens size, depth of field and camera shake. It adds text-to-speech dialogue, facial expression tools, drawing and text annotation, a production slate, and imports of 3D objects, audio, images and characters. Optional paid expansions cover Augmented Reality, Face Mocap, Post FX Pro and Character Designer.

§19 Screenwriting & development tools (including AI coverage/analysis and script clearance/title research) ⟦S19⟧

Market read · The defining event in this category is consolidation followed by collapse. Cast & Crew — a production payroll and accounting company — acquired Final Draft in February 2016, then picked up Coverfly, FilmFreeway, ScreenCraft, WeScreenplay and The Script Lab via its 2022 Backstage purchase, running them as Industry Arts. In 2025 it shut four of them: WeScreenplay (Jan 31), ScreenCraft and The Script Lab (Feb 28), Coverfly (Aug 1). No Film School called it the end of the coverage industry. The Black List inherited a near-monopoly on industry-readable hosting at roughly $30/month plus $100 per evaluation, with only Stage 32 beside it. That matters to Cinamate two ways: the screenwriting-tools layer is owned by the same company whose payroll rails The Money Room competes with, and that owner has shown it will kill adjacent properties. Pricing has bifurcated violently. Writing itself is now free-to-$126/year — Beat and Trelby at $0, Fountain as a vendor-neutral format, Arc Studio at $69/year, WriterDuet at $89.88/year, Fade In at $79.95 once, STARC at $150 lifetime. Script analysis collapsed from the $89-$150 WeScreenplay era to $9.99-$29 (ScriptReader.ai, StoryNotes, OnDesk). Neither the writer room nor bundled coverage can be a Cinamate differentiator at those prices. The money has moved to pipeline: FinalBit (ex-Nolan AI) at $40-$100/month and RivetAI at $49.99-$150 per project both sell script-to-shoot-ready, and RivetAI is the sharpest threat — same one-screenplay-drives-everything thesis, plus RBAC, MFA, SSO, a REST API, an MCP connector, patent claims and a written no-AI-training commitment. It answers the studio security review Cinamate cannot yet pass. Two Cinamate claims are directly contested. Its sales model faces Largo (three granted patents, EPFL-based) and ScriptBook (studio-facing since 2014) — though neither publishes a failure rate, so Cinamate's disclosed 15.5% with P10-P90 bands is genuinely more transparent, and worth leading with. Its clearance room faces a harder wall: The Clearance Lab charges $10-$15 per page and $399-$799 for title reports, and Act One has been issuing De Forest Reports since 1952. Those outputs are what E&O carriers and distributors accept. Software cannot substitute for them, and positioning the clearance room as a pre-clearance triage that reduces billable pages is far safer than implying it replaces them. Finally, competitors have already closed two of Cinamate's named gaps: Arc Studio and Highland Pro ship real iPhone/iPad apps, and Celtx ships an Adobe Premiere Pro plugin. Meanwhile ScreenWeaver, an open beta, has named festival awards (Seoul International AI Film Festival, Mondial Chroma) for films made in it — external validation Cinamate lacks while press declines and the product sits invite-only on a netlify.app subdomain.
Final Draft (Cast & Crew) www.finaldraft.com DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
The incumbent screenplay file format and production-office standard, owned by the payroll company whose rails Cinamate's Money Room is trying to replace.

Final Draft is the long-standing industry-standard screenwriting application, currently at version 13, with a Final Draft Suite subscription that pairs a browser-based Final Draft Cloud with the desktop app. It markets Beat Board outlining, collaboration and table-read features, and claims use by 95% of film and TV professionals. Strategically the more important fact is ownership: Cast & Crew acquired Final Draft in February 2016, and Cast & Crew also owns FilmFreeway, the Big Break contest, and — via its 2022 Backstage acquisition — the Industry Arts group that ran Coverfly, ScreenCraft, WeScreenplay and The Script Lab before shutting all four down in 2025. Cast & Crew's core business is production payroll and accounting (PSL), which is the same ground as Cinamate's Money Room.

Key features ·  Industry-standard .fdx format and formatting engine · Beat Board and outlining · Collaboration and table reads · Final Draft Cloud (browser) plus desktop · Revision modes, production locking, reports · Studio/production volume licensing and educational licensing
Pricing Final Draft 13 Personal $199.99 (listed down from $249.99); Student $99.99 (from $129.99); Upgrade $79.99 (from $129.99). Final Draft Suite subscription "as low as USD $8.33/month" billed yearly. Educators/non-profits and studios/production: custom pricing via sales.
Scale & ownership Owned by Cast & Crew (acquisition announced February 2016; Cast & Crew founded 1976, HQ Burbank). Claims 95% market share among film/TV professionals. Cast & Crew's portfolio includes FilmFreeway, Backstage, Big Break, and the now-shuttered Industry Arts coverage properties. Revenue and unit numbers not disclosed.

RivetAI rivetai.com/en DIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
Per-project pre-production platform where script, breakdown, schedule, budget and coverage all run off one screenplay.

RivetAI positions itself as "all-in-one pre-production infrastructure" for film and TV: an industry-standard script editor with scene tagging and revision tracking, AI scene/character breakdown, AI coverage reports, stripboards and DOOD scheduling, budget top sheets with line items, and tax-incentive scenarios — all reading the same draft with no file handoffs. A cohort of AI coverage tools that filled the vacuum left by the 2025 Industry Arts shutdowns. ScriptReader.ai runs five independent AI readers plus a synthesis, with a "Layered Read" grading acts, sequences and scenes separately, a coverage grid, scene-by-scene notes, and a generated poster and narrated pitch video. Open-source and free screenwriting stack (Fountain, Beat, Trelby, Story Architect/STARC) www.beat-app.fi INDIRECT LOW VERIFIED
A credible $0 floor for the writer room, anchored by the Fountain plain-text format that everything else already supports.

Fountain is an open plain-text screenplay markup that decouples screenplays from any vendor. Beat is a fully open-source, elegant macOS screenwriting app built on Fountain, created by a screenwriter, with a JavaScript plugin architecture, local-only file storage, offline operation and a Patreon funding model — free on macOS, €12.99 on iOS. Trelby is free multiplatform software with a screenplay editor enforcing correct format and pagination, auto-completion, spell check, draft/WYSIWYG/fullscreen views, a 200,000-name character name database, scene/location/character/dialogue reports, script comparison, and import/export across FDX, Celtx, Fountain, Adobe Story and Fade In. STARC (Story Architect, the successor to KIT Scenarist) covers screenplays, comics, audio dramas, stageplays and novels in one project bible with mind maps, corkboard, timeline, character relations editor, location maps and a ChatGPT-based AI assistant.

§20 Indirect substitutes and the do-nothing option ⟦S20⟧

Market read · This is the category Cinamate actually loses in. There is no market leader here because the category is not a market - it is the absence of one. The default indie production stack is Google Sheets + WhatsApp + Google Drive + a free Wrapbook or StudioBinder template + a $20/month AI assistant, and it costs roughly $0-500 for an entire feature. Cinamate's own quoted figure of ~$110 per 90-page feature render (unverified figure) is competitive on render, but the 28 surrounding modules are competing against free. Pricing norms: horizontal SaaS clusters at $5-25/seat/month (Trello $5, ClickUp $7, Notion $10, Asana $10.99, Monday $9-19, Airtable $20-45 - all verified annual rates). Film-specific point tools are cheap where they are self-serve (Saturation.io $32-79/mo, Croogloo $19-999/mo) and opaque where they are services (Cast & Crew, GreenSlate, Wrapbook, Movie Magic - all pricing on request). Direction of travel is against Cinamate: every horizontal tool shipped an AI layer in 2025-26 (Notion Business $20 with Notion Agent, ClickUp Everything AI $28, Monday's AI agent workforce), so the "AI does your breakdown" pitch is no longer differentiating. Consolidation is happening in payroll/accounting (Cast & Crew absorbed Showbiz Software; EP owns Movie Magic), not in producer tooling. What this means for Cinamate: the buyer is not choosing between Cinamate and LightsKiddo. They are choosing between Cinamate and a spreadsheet they already trust, plus a line producer whose judgment they trust more. An invite-only beta on a netlify.app subdomain with no public team, no SOC 2, no TPN and no mobile app has to beat "free and familiar" on trust, not on feature count - and 28 modules is a switching-cost argument against itself.
Doing nothing (email + PDF + paper + the producer's own head) unknown INDIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
The single largest competitor in the category: no tool at all, because the producer has made films this way before.

On most independent films the actual system is: a budget spreadsheet emailed as an attachment, a schedule PDF emailed the night before, call sheets printed and handed out at crew park, deal memos signed on paper or as scanned PDFs, releases in a folder in the AD's bag, and every decision that matters held in the producer's and line producer's heads. This is not laziness - it is a rational response to a market where the tooling changes every two years, the crew turns over every project, and the film has a fixed 30-day life. Nothing to learn, nothing to pay for, nothing to migrate, nothing to lose when the vendor pivots.

Key features ·  Zero cost, zero learning curve, zero vendor risk · Works with any crew member on any device with no account · Formats every department already recognizes: PDF call sheet, printed sides, emailed budget · No data-security exposure to a third-party beta product · Survives the production - the PDFs are still readable in ten years
Pricing $0 in software. The real cost is human: duplicated data entry, version-control errors, late cost information, and the producer's time. That cost is invisible on the budget top sheet, which is precisely why it persists.
Scale & ownership Not measurable as a product, but by inference the dominant behaviour: the persistence of free template libraries (Wrapbook's 100+ downloads, StudioBinder's Google Sheets budget, SAGindie's sample agreements) exists because the demand is for documents, not systems.
Collides with ·  All 28 modules · The Money Room · Studio Cloud Backup · workflow · today · projects

  • No trust question about a netlify.app subdomain, no public team, no SOC 2, no TPN and declined press coverage
  • No 9h 12m render, no local GPU requirement, no single-operator constraint

A $20/month chatbot that will break down a script, draft a schedule, estimate a budget and write a deal memo on demand.

This is the substitute that has changed most since 2024 and the one that most directly attacks Cinamate's reason to exist. A producer pastes a screenplay into Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini and gets a scene-by-scene element breakdown, a day-out-of-days, a rough budget in an account structure, a location list, a props and wardrobe list, a safety-flag pass, deal memo drafts, festival strategy and a tax-credit comparison - conversationally, in an afternoon, with no invite code and no GPU. Long-context models handle a full 110-page screenplay in a single prompt. All three now have file upload, spreadsheet output and web search for verifying current union rates.

Excel is where the overwhelming majority of independent film budgets, stripboards, PO logs, cost reports and cash-flow schedules actually live. Producers use inherited .xlsx templates - passed down from a previous production, a film school, a line producer, or a free download - with account-code structures mirroring Movie Magic's 1100/2000/6000 series. It handles budgeting, actuals-vs-estimate cost reporting, crew lists, and petty cash without any vendor relationship. Every financier, completion bond company and bank in the business can open the file.

Hiring a freelance line producer / UPM / production accountant www.producersguild.org INDIRECT HIGH UNCERTAIN
Buying a person's judgment and relationships instead of software - still the default for any film with real money in it.

The single most common answer to "how do I budget and schedule this film" is: hire someone who has done it thirty times. A line producer produces the budget and schedule, negotiates crew and vendor deals, and carries the relationships that actually determine what a production costs. A production accountant runs the cost report, PO log, payroll interface and the tax-credit audit trail. A UPM runs the office. These people arrive with their own Movie Magic or Excel templates, their own vendor rate cards, and - critically - the credibility that gets a completion bond issued and a financier's signature.

Key features ·  Human judgment on what a scene actually costs in a specific city with a specific crew · Vendor and crew relationships that convert directly into rate discounts · Credibility with financiers, bond companies and studio execs that no software has · Carries legal and professional accountability for the numbers · Adapts in real time on set - no app required
Pricing Not disclosed as a published figure; rates are negotiated per project and vary widely by budget tier, territory and union status. Attempts to verify specific weekly rates via Wrapbook, Glassdoor, Backstage and Upwork all returned HTTP 403/404 in this pass - treat any rate range as unverified. Directionally, this is the most expensive substitute in the category by an order of magnitude, and producers buy it anyway.
Scale & ownership The Producers Guild of America maintains eligibility standards, a Producers Mark (p.g.a.) certification, Hire PGA job listings, mentoring programs and a member resource library - membership dues not disclosed. This is an established professional class, not a product category.

§21 Content security, compliance & the buying gate ⟦S21⟧

Market read · This category is not a competitor set — it is the turnstile. Nothing here sells what Cinamate sells; everything here decides whether Cinamate is allowed to sell at all. The gate is a stack, and Cinamate currently fails at four different heights: TPN/MPA Best Practices (may you touch pre-release footage), SOC 2 (will procurement clear you), the union layer (may the output be used on a covered production), and the US Copyright Office (can the output be owned, insured and distributed). A vendor can be excellent and still be un-buyable. Two findings change the picture. First, TPN replaced its two-tier model with four tiers at MPA Best Practices v5.3.1 — and the new Blue Shield is self-assessed, published to the TPN+ registry, and costs only membership. At Cinamate's revenue that is $250-$1,000/year with no third-party auditor. That is the cheapest credibility Cinamate can buy, and LightsKiddo's "TPN assessment in progress" would be answerable in weeks, not quarters. Second, the secure-review layer has consolidated hard: PIX and Moxion are now both Autodesk Flow Capture, Shift.io now redirects to MediaSilo. Frame.io Enterprise publicly claims TPN+ Gold Shield and SOC 2 Type 2 — that is the bar buyers now quote. The deepest gate cannot be bought around. Copyright Office Part 2 (Jan 2025) holds that purely AI-generated output is unregistrable. No registration means no clean chain of title, no E&O binder, no distribution — which lands directly on Studio/Local Generation, clearance, contracts and distribution. Meanwhile EU AI Act Article 50 entered into force three weeks ago (2 Aug 2026), making machine-readable synthetic-content marking a shipping requirement in Europe today.
MPA Content Security Best Practices (v5.3.1) www.ttpn.org/faqs INDIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
The single benchmark of minimum security preparedness for the content industries — the control set every TPN assessment scores against.

The MPA Content Security Best Practices are maintained by TPN on behalf of the Motion Picture Association and establish, in TPN's own words, 'a single benchmark of minimum security preparedness for content industries.' They are the control catalogue against which a TPN questionnaire and assessment are scored. The current release driving the new four-tier Shield program is v5.3.1. Aspects of a provider's security not fully in conformance are recorded as remediation items rather than failures.

Key features ·  Maintained by TPN, published under MPA authority · Current version v5.3.1, which triggered the migration from two Shield tiers to four · Covers site security, cloud security and application security as separately assessable domains · Conformance is expressed as remediation items, not a pass/fail score · Remediation is reviewed by TPN SecOps against submitted evidence · Referenced by content owners as the baseline in vendor security questionnaires and MSAs
Pricing The Best Practices documents themselves are published reference material and are not sold; the cost is TPN membership plus a separately contracted third-party assessment. TPN does not publish assessment pricing.
Scale & ownership Industry-wide baseline across the MPA member studios and the broader content supply chain; global applicability. The MPA's Content Security Initiative published a 2026 report linking control failures to content security incidents across the entertainment industry.
Collides with ·  Studio Cloud Backup — encryption at rest/in transit, key management, retention and deletion controls are all explicit Best Practices items · Studio/Local Generation — endpoint hardening, removable-media policy and physical security of the local GPU workstation · The Cutting Room — session controls, watermarking, download restriction and screenshot prevention for browser review of pre-release picture · tools (slate/timecards/LUT preview), today, production — on-set data handling and asset custody controls · contracts and clearance — the Best Practices require documented third-party/subcontractor management, which a single-operator vendor still must evidence
Stronger than Cinamate
  • It is buyer-authored, so it defines the vocabulary of every security conversation Cinamate will have
  • It assumes an organization with policies, named security roles, incident response and personnel screening — a product with no public team cannot evidence most of that
  • LightsKiddo's foundry model of embedding engineers with productions maps naturally onto Best Practices personnel and training controls
Weaker than Cinamate
  • It is a controls checklist, not a product; it competes with nothing Cinamate builds and can be satisfied by documentation and process rather than engineering
  • Many controls are scoped out or marked not-applicable for a small application provider, so the real burden is far smaller than the document length suggests
  • It is architecture-neutral: Cinamate's local-only generation genuinely reduces exposure even though the framework gives no explicit credit for it
https://www.ttpn.org/faqs/ · https://www.ttpn.org/ · https://www.ttpn.org/links-resources/
SAG-AFTRA AI consent and digital-replica terms www.sagaftra.org/contracts-industry-resources/contracts/artificial-intelligence INDIRECT CRITICAL LIKELY
The performers' union rules requiring informed consent and compensation for digital replicas — the reason a Cinamate-generated performance cannot lawfully appear in a union production without paperwork.

SAG-AFTRA's agreements govern the use of AI-generated and AI-altered performances on covered productions. The union's framework distinguishes employment-based digital replicas (created from a performer's work on a production) from independently created digital replicas, and separately addresses synthetic performers not based on any single individual. Consent must be informed and specific, and compensation is owed for replica use. The union's willingness to enforce is demonstrated: SAG-AFTRA filed an unfair labor practice charge in May 2025 over the AI-generated Darth Vader voice in Fortnite, and its Interactive Media (video game) strike ran from 26 July 2024 to 9 July 2025 specifically over AI protections, ending with an agreement ratified on 9 July 2025 that secured digital-replica terms.

Key features ·  Informed, specific consent required before creating or using a digital replica · Separate treatment of employment-based replicas, independently created replicas and synthetic performers · Compensation owed for digital-replica use, not covered by the original engagement fee · Notice and bargaining obligations around synthetic performers · Enforcement is active: ULP charge filed May 2025 over AI Darth Vader voice in Fortnite · Interactive Media Agreement AI terms won after a nearly year-long strike (26 Jul 2024 - 9 Jul 2025), ratified 9 July 2025 · Union-side side deals with AI voice vendors (e.g. Replica Studios Jan 2024, Ethovox Oct 2024) show a licensed-path model exists
Pricing Not applicable — collective bargaining agreement. Cinamate's own brief cites SAG-AFTRA daily scale of $1,246 for 2025-26; replica consent and usage compensation are negotiated on top of scale and are not a published rate card.
Scale & ownership SAG-AFTRA covers approximately 160,000 performers across film, television, streaming, commercials, audiobooks and interactive media (membership figure from background knowledge, not verified on a page I loaded). Signatory status is required for essentially every professional US live-action production.
Collides with ·  Studio/Local Generation — generating performances script-to-screen is exactly the activity the digital-replica and synthetic-performer rules govern · casting — the module that engages performers is where consent capture must live, and it currently has no described consent artifact · contracts / deal memos — replica consent riders are now standard and must be generated, stored and produced on demand · clearance — performer likeness rights are a core clearance item for any AI-generated face or voice · producer (budget/stripboard) and finance — replica compensation is a budget line Cinamate's cost model must carry · distribution deliverables — distributors demand warranties that union AI terms were honored
Stronger than Cinamate
  • It is enforceable through grievance and arbitration, with a demonstrated willingness to strike for a year over exactly this issue
  • It applies to the productions Cinamate targets — independent producers and small studios still sign union agreements
  • LightsKiddo's live-action, crew-facing positioning largely avoids the synthetic-performer problem; Cinamate's core product is the problem
  • No security certification or engineering effort mitigates it
Weaker than Cinamate
  • It is a consent-and-compensation regime, not a prohibition — fully licensed synthetic performance is contemplated and already happening via union-sanctioned vendor deals

The MPA-owned content-security registry and assessment program that most studios and streamers use as a precondition for handing a vendor pre-release content.

TPN is wholly owned by the Motion Picture Association. It maintains the MPA Content Security Best Practices, runs security assessments measuring a service provider's posture against them, and operates TPN+, a global registry where providers publish their security status to content owners. Critically, TPN explicitly does NOT certify or issue pass/fail grades — it publishes conformance data and remediation items, and content owners make their own risk-based sourcing decisions. As of the v5.3.1 questionnaire, TPN replaced its two-tier Blue/Gold model with four tiers.

US Copyright Office — AI guidance (Reports Parts 1-3) www.copyright.gov/ai INDIRECT CRITICAL VERIFIED
The federal position that human authorship is required for copyright — the gate that determines whether a Cinamate-generated film can be owned, insured and distributed at all.

The Copyright Office has issued a multi-part report on copyright and AI. Part 1, Digital Replicas (31 July 2024), recommends federal digital-replica legislation. Part 2, Copyrightability (29 January 2025), examines whether generative-AI outputs can receive copyright protection. Part 3, Generative AI Training, was released in prepublication form on 9 May 2025 with a final version expected without substantive change. The Office's operative principle is that copyright protects human authorship: works generated entirely by AI without meaningful human creative input are not registrable, though hybrid works may be protected for their human-authored portions. Registration requires disclosure of AI-generated content.

Key features ·  Part 1 Digital Replicas — 31 July 2024 · Part 2 Copyrightability — 29 January 2025 · Part 3 Generative AI Training — prepublication 9 May 2025 · Registration applicants must disclose AI-generated content in the deposit · Human-authored elements may be registrable; AI-generated portions cannot be · Purely AI-generated works are ineligible for registration · Guidance, not statute — but it governs the registration decision, which is what downstream commerce depends on
Pricing Not applicable — federal agency guidance. Copyright registration fees are separate statutory filing fees.
Scale & ownership US federal agency within the Library of Congress; its registration decisions bind the US market and are the reference point for E&O insurers, distributors and financiers worldwide.
Collides with ·  Studio/Local Generation — this is the direct hit: a 90-page feature rendered script-to-screen for ~$110 is precisely the output whose copyrightability is in question · writer — AI-generated screenplay material raises the same authorship problem at the source of the chain of title · clearance — the module that is supposed to certify a clean chain of title cannot certify one that does not exist · contracts / deal memos — assignment of rights presumes there are rights to assign · distribution deliverables and festivals — distributors and festivals require chain-of-title documentation and E&O coverage, both of which trace back to registrability · investors and finance — an unregistrable asset is far harder to collateralize or waterfall
Stronger than Cinamate

  • It attacks the flagship claim directly: 'turns a screenplay into a finished film' describes exactly the output most at risk of being held unprotectable
  • LightsKiddo's positioning around live-action crews with camera integrations sidesteps this entirely, because human-shot footage is unambiguously authored
Weaker than Cinamate
  • It does not prohibit anything — it governs registration, so AI-assisted work is legal to make and distribute, just harder to protect
  • Hybrid works with meaningful human authorship are registrable, and Cinamate is a 28-module pipeline where a human operator makes thousands of creative decisions — that is a defensible authorship narrative if documented
  • The disclosure requirement is a documentation problem, and Cinamate already has provenance-adjacent infrastructure (workflow, timeline, projects) that could produce an authorship record
  • Part 3 remains prepublication, and the law here is unsettled and actively litigated

C2PA / Content Credentials c2pa.org INDIRECT HIGH VERIFIED
The open provenance standard — and, since the EU AI Act took effect, the most practical way to satisfy machine-readable synthetic-content marking.

C2PA, the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity, publishes an open technical standard letting publishers, creators and consumers establish the origin and edit history of digital content. The user-facing manifestation is Content Credentials, described as a nutrition label for digital content. The current specification line is 2.x, with version 2.3 published. In mid-2025 C2PA launched a formal Conformance Program and the official C2PA Trust List, retiring the earlier Interim Trust List that had operated through 31 December 2025; the new Trust List adds a public Certificate Policy for CAs, stronger governance, alignment with the 2.x specification series, and Time Stamping Authority trust lists.

Key features ·  Open specification, current version 2.3 · C2PA Conformance Program and official C2PA Trust List launched mid-2025 · Interim Trust List retired after 31 December 2025 · Public Certificate Policy specifying requirements for Certification Authorities · Time Stamping Authority trust lists for generator products · Cryptographically signed manifests recording origin and edit history · Durable credentials paired with invisible watermarking and fingerprinting in some implementations, so credentials survive stripping or screenshotting
Pricing The specification is open and free to implement. Certificate issuance under the Conformance Program runs through participating Certification Authorities; CA pricing is not disclosed on the C2PA site.
Scale & ownership Steering committee of eleven organizations: Adobe, Amazon, BBC, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Publicis Groupe, Sony Group, TikTok and Truepic. The Content Credentials project reports collaboration with 500+ companies.
Collides with ·  The Cutting Room — H.264+AAC export and EDL/OTIO conform are where C2PA manifests would need to be written and preserved · Studio/Local Generation — the generator product is the entity that would hold a C2PA certificate and sign its output · distribution deliverables — provenance manifests are becoming a delivery spec item · dailies, editor, post, vfx — every transform step must carry the manifest forward or the chain breaks · Studio Cloud Backup — a natural place to store the signed provenance ledger across the production state · workflow and projects — Cinamate's existing workflow tracking is the raw material for a credible authorship/provenance record
Stronger than Cinamate

  • It is the de facto answer to EU AI Act Article 50 machine-readable marking, which is now in force
  • The Conformance Program means ad-hoc implementations no longer count — there is a real certificate and trust-list gate now
  • Adobe ships Content Credentials in the tools Cinamate's users already touch
Weaker than Cinamate
  • It is an open standard, free to implement, and imposes no membership fee — this is the cheapest compliance win available to Cinamate
  • Implementation is a bounded engineering task in the export path, not an organizational certification
  • Provenance signing would actively help Cinamate's copyrightability story by documenting human creative decisions across 28 modules

California AB 1836 — digital replicas of deceased personalities leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240AB1836 INDIRECT HIGH VERIFIED
California law requiring estate consent before using a digital replica of a deceased performer, with statutory damages — a liability trap for any generative film tool.

AB 1836, approved 17 September 2024, requires anyone producing, distributing or making available a digital replica of a deceased personality's voice or likeness in an audiovisual work or sound recording to obtain prior consent from authorized representatives of the estate. Liability is the greater of $10,000 or actual damages to the rights holder, plus available punitive damages and mandatory attorney's fees and costs to the prevailing party. Protection runs for 70 years after death. Exemptions cover news, public affairs and sports broadcasts; comment, criticism, scholarship, satire and parody; documentary, historical or biographical works unless falsely presented as an authentic recording; fleeting or incidental appearances; and advertisements for those exempt works. Authorized digital remastering and sampling are excluded.

Key features ·  Prior consent from the estate's authorized representative required · Damages: greater of $10,000 or actual damages, plus punitive damages · Mandatory attorney's fees and costs to the prevailing party · 70-year post-mortem term · Exemptions for news, criticism, satire, parody, documentary/historical/biographical use, and fleeting appearances · Approved 17 September 2024 · Same digital-replica definition as AB 2602
Pricing Not applicable — state statute.
Scale & ownership California state law with national practical reach given where entertainment contracts and productions are centered; estates of deceased performers are actively represented and litigious.
Collides with ·  Studio/Local Generation — a text prompt naming a deceased actor produces exactly the prohibited artifact, and the system as described has no gate preventing it · casting — no described mechanism for detecting or blocking a deceased-personality likeness request · clearance — the module nominally responsible for rights clearance would need an estate-consent workflow and a deceased-personality screen · contracts / deal memos — estate consent instruments are a distinct document class not described in Cinamate's contract coverage · distribution deliverables and festivals — distributors will demand a warranty that no unlicensed digital replica appears in the master · The Cutting Room and post — the liability attaches to distributing or making available, so it survives into delivery
Stronger than Cinamate
  • Statutory damages plus mandatory fee-shifting make even a small violation economically serious for a small vendor or a single operator
  • Fully automated generation with no likeness screen is a structural exposure: the tool will produce violations if asked
  • LightsKiddo's live-action camera-ingest positioning does not generate likenesses at all, so it carries none of this risk
Weaker than Cinamate
  • The exemption list is broad — documentary, biographical, satire and parody uses cover a meaningful share of independent filmmaking
  • Liability attaches to the producer/distributor, not automatically to the tool vendor
  • A deceased-personality name screen in casting and clearance is a tractable feature, and shipping one would be a genuine trust signal
  • Only applies to replicas readily identifiable as a specific real individual; wholly synthetic characters are untouched
